flashcards.back: A user-driven profile lets an end user unbox a device, sign in with their own Microsoft Entra ID account, and finish provisioning themselves. A self-deploying profile needs no user interaction at all and authenticates the device itself, commonly for kiosks or shared devices. A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile lets a partner or IT do the time-consuming steps in advance, so the end user only completes a short final phase.
flashcards.detail: Self-deploying profiles require a TPM 2.0 device that can authenticate on its own, since there is no user present to sign in and prove identity. Whichever profile is used, the Enrollment Status Page (ESP) is what actually blocks the desktop until provisioning finishes.

flashcards.front: Windows Autopilot device preparation vs classic Autopilot
flashcards.back: Windows Autopilot device preparation is the newer, streamlined cloud-native provisioning path, built for speed and simplified Entra-joined deployment with tighter Intune integration. Classic Autopilot deployment profiles (user-driven, self-deploying, pre-provisioned) remain available for hybrid Entra join and scenarios device preparation does not yet cover.
flashcards.detail: Device preparation is Microsoft's direction going forward, but it currently only supports Microsoft Entra joined devices, not hybrid Entra join, so classic profiles still matter for hybrid environments.

flashcards.back: A provisioning policy defines how a Cloud PC is created: which Microsoft Entra ID group receives it, the image used, the Entra join type (Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid Entra joined), and the domain join configuration. It is what actually triggers Cloud PC creation once a user is licensed and assigned.
flashcards.detail: A user needs both a Windows 365 license assignment and a matching provisioning policy scope; having only one of the two never results in a Cloud PC being created.

flashcards.back: Windows 365 Enterprise licenses one Cloud PC per named user for dedicated, always-on use. Windows 365 Frontline licenses a smaller pool of Cloud PCs shared across a larger set of shift-based users, with only a limited number of concurrent connections allowed per license set.
flashcards.detail: Frontline is the cost-effective pick for shift workers who never overlap, since three Frontline licenses can serve far more than three named users as long as no more than three connect at once.

flashcards.back: Windows Autopatch is a managed service that takes over update deployment for enrolled devices, automatically organizing them into deployment rings and rolling out Windows quality updates, driver and firmware updates, Microsoft 365 Apps updates, and Edge updates on Microsoft-managed schedules.
flashcards.detail: Enrolling a device in Autopatch requires it already be Intune-managed, licensed appropriately (such as Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5), and meeting prerequisite checks the Autopatch readiness assessment reports on.

flashcards.back: Hotpatching applies a subset of security updates to a running Windows instance in memory, without requiring the usual reboot that full monthly cumulative updates need, reducing downtime and restart fatigue for enrolled devices.
flashcards.detail: Hotpatch releases still land on a baseline cumulative update periodically, since not every fix can be applied in memory, so it reduces reboots rather than eliminating them entirely.

flashcards.back: Windows devices can be enrolled through Windows Autopilot, Group Policy-based auto-enrollment for already domain-joined devices, a bulk enrollment provisioning package built with Windows Configuration Designer, or manual self-enrollment through Settings for a device already Entra joined or registered.
flashcards.detail: GPO-based auto-enrollment is specifically for hybrid Entra joined devices that are already domain-joined and simply need to pick up MDM enrollment automatically, rather than a from-scratch provisioning method.

flashcards.front: Windows Update for Business update rings
flashcards.back: An update ring is an Intune policy that controls when and how a group of devices receives quality and feature updates: deferral periods, whether updates install automatically, active hours, and whether the device is part of an early or broad deployment wave.
flashcards.detail: Rings are commonly staged, with a small pilot ring using a short or zero deferral and progressively larger rings using longer deferrals, so a bad update is caught on a small population before it reaches everyone.

flashcards.front: Feature update deferral vs quality update deferral
flashcards.back: A feature update deferral delays a new Windows version, such as moving from one annual release to the next, by up to 365 days. A quality update deferral delays monthly, cumulative security and reliability fixes by up to 30 days. They are configured and deferred independently of each other in the same update ring.
flashcards.detail: Delaying feature updates does not delay quality updates on the same ring, so a device can still be receiving this month's security patches on a much older feature version.

flashcards.front: Co-management workloads and the co-management slider
flashcards.back: Co-management lets a hybrid Entra joined device be managed by both Configuration Manager and Intune at once. Per-workload sliders, such as Compliance policies, Device Configuration, or Windows Update Policies, individually decide whether Configuration Manager or Intune is authoritative for that specific workload.
flashcards.detail: Switching a workload's slider to Intune does not uninstall or disable the Configuration Manager client; Configuration Manager still manages every workload whose slider was not moved.

flashcards.back: A safeguard hold automatically blocks a feature update from being offered to a device that Microsoft has detected has a known compatibility issue, preventing the upgrade until Microsoft resolves the issue and lifts the hold, or an administrator explicitly overrides it in Intune.
flashcards.detail: Safeguard holds are Microsoft's own protective mechanism, not something an admin configures directly, though Intune does surface which devices are held and lets an admin choose to bypass one deliberately.

flashcards.back: MDM authority determines which management service is in charge of a tenant's mobile device management. Modern Intune tenants use Intune Standalone as sole MDM authority; a legacy configuration where Configuration Manager alone held that authority is largely obsolete now that co-management is the standard hybrid approach.
flashcards.detail: A tenant with no MDM authority set at all cannot enroll any devices, which is one of the first things to check when enrollment silently fails tenant-wide.

flashcards.front: Enrollment restrictions: platform vs device limit
flashcards.back: A device platform restriction blocks or allows enrollment by OS type, such as Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, or macOS, and can require a minimum or maximum OS version. A device limit restriction caps how many devices a single user is allowed to enroll, independent of platform.
flashcards.detail: Restrictions are evaluated in priority order like Conditional Access policies; the most specific, highest-priority restriction assigned to a user or group wins, with a built-in default restriction applying to everyone else.

flashcards.front: Device configuration profiles vs the settings catalog
flashcards.back: Older, template-based device configuration profiles group related settings into purpose-built templates, such as Endpoint Protection or Device restrictions. The settings catalog instead exposes essentially every available CSP-backed setting individually, searchable and combinable into one custom profile.
flashcards.detail: Microsoft has been steering new profile creation toward the settings catalog because it always reflects the latest available settings, while some older templates are no longer being updated with new options.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Entra device states: joined, hybrid joined, and registered
flashcards.back: A Microsoft Entra joined device is owned by the organization and knows only Entra ID, with no on-premises AD account. A hybrid Entra joined device is joined to on-premises AD and also registered with Entra ID. A Microsoft Entra registered device is typically a personal or BYOD device that has only added an Entra ID account without full organizational join.
flashcards.detail: Only a joined or hybrid joined device can enforce a full set of Intune device-level compliance and configuration policies the same way; a registered BYOD device is generally managed through mobile application management instead.

flashcards.back: Intune device management is included in Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Enterprise Mobility + Security (EMS) E3/E5, or as a standalone Intune Plan license. Windows 365 Cloud PC requires its own separate per-user Cloud PC license, Enterprise or Frontline, layered on top of whatever license already provides the user's Intune management.
flashcards.detail: A user without an Intune-capable license can still technically be assigned policy, but their devices will not actually enroll or receive it; licensing gates enrollment itself, not just policy delivery.

flashcards.back: A scope tag limits which Intune administrators can see and manage a given policy, app, or device, letting role-based delegation, such as a regional helpdesk team, apply only to objects tagged for their scope, instead of the entire tenant's configuration.
flashcards.detail: Scope tags control visibility and management rights for admins; they do not change which end users or devices a policy is assigned to and applies against.

flashcards.front: The Intune Connector for Active Directory
flashcards.back: The Intune Connector for Active Directory is an on-premises agent that lets Autopilot hybrid Entra join create the computer object in on-premises AD during provisioning, bridging cloud-based Autopilot provisioning with an on-premises domain join step.
flashcards.detail: Without this connector installed and healthy, a hybrid Entra join Autopilot profile fails at the domain-join stage even though every other Autopilot configuration is correct.

flashcards.front: Configuration profile assignment conflicts and filters
flashcards.back: When two assigned configuration profiles set the same setting differently for the same device, Intune reports a conflict and neither value is applied for that setting until the conflict is resolved. Assignment filters narrow which devices in an assigned group actually receive a profile, app, or policy, based on device properties like OS version or manufacturer.
flashcards.detail: A filter is applied on top of a group assignment, not instead of it; a device must both be in the assigned group and match the filter to receive the item.

flashcards.front: Compliance policy settings and actions for noncompliance
flashcards.back: A compliance policy defines requirements a device must meet, such as minimum OS version, encryption, or a passcode. Actions for noncompliance define what happens when a device fails, on an escalating schedule: send an email, mark the device noncompliant immediately, and eventually block access via Conditional Access if not remediated within a grace period.
flashcards.detail: Marking a device noncompliant and blocking its Conditional Access access are two separate, sequenced actions; a device can be flagged noncompliant while still inside its grace period before access is actually blocked.

flashcards.front: Conditional Access grant control: require device to be marked compliant
flashcards.back: The require device to be marked as compliant grant control in Conditional Access checks the device's compliance status recorded by Intune at sign-in time, blocking access unless that specific device, not just any device belonging to the user, is currently compliant.
flashcards.detail: This grant control is device-bound, not user-bound; a compliant device satisfies it even for a risky sign-in location, while the same user on a noncompliant personal device is blocked even from a trusted network.

flashcards.front: Onboarding devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint via Intune
flashcards.back: Intune can push a Defender for Endpoint onboarding configuration profile to enrolled devices, connecting them to the Defender for Endpoint service so their risk signals flow back into Intune and can feed device compliance policies based on machine risk level.
flashcards.detail: Once connected, a compliance policy can require a maximum allowed device risk score from Defender for Endpoint, letting a device that becomes actively compromised automatically fail compliance and lose Conditional Access-gated access.

flashcards.back: A security baseline is a Microsoft-curated group of preconfigured settings, based on Microsoft-recommended and industry-standard values, that can be assigned as a starting point and then customized, instead of building an equivalent settings catalog profile completely from scratch.
flashcards.detail: Baselines are versioned; a newer baseline version can introduce new or changed default settings, and an admin must explicitly move a profile instance to the new version to actually pick up those changes.

flashcards.front: BitLocker and disk encryption policy via Intune
flashcards.back: An endpoint protection or settings catalog encryption profile can require BitLocker on a Windows device, control recovery key storage in Microsoft Entra ID, silently enable encryption without prompting the user, and specify the encryption method and cipher strength.
flashcards.detail: Storing the recovery key in Microsoft Entra ID lets a help desk technician look it up during a self-service or assisted recovery, without the end user ever having written it down themselves.

flashcards.back: Endpoint Privilege Management lets a standard, non-administrator user elevate specific, approved applications to run with administrator rights, without granting that user full local administrator rights on the device at all.
flashcards.detail: EPM elevation rules can require the user to supply a business justification, or route the request through Microsoft Entra ID-integrated approval, before the elevation is actually granted for that one application.

flashcards.back: Attack surface reduction rules, delivered through Intune endpoint security policy, target specific, commonly exploited behaviors, such as Office apps creating child processes or credential theft from LSASS, and can block, audit, or warn on them independent of full antivirus signature detection.
flashcards.detail: Deploying ASR rules in audit mode first, and reviewing the resulting events, is the recommended way to find false positives before actually enforcing block mode against a production population.

flashcards.front: Intune app deployment intents: required, available, and uninstall
flashcards.back: A required assignment installs an app automatically on every targeted device or user with no action needed. An available assignment lists the app in the Company Portal so a user can choose to install it. An uninstall assignment removes the app from targeted devices or users.
flashcards.detail: An app can carry different intents for different assigned groups simultaneously; required for one department's group while merely available for everyone else.

flashcards.front: App protection policies (MAM) vs mobile device management
flashcards.back: An app protection policy applies data-protection controls, like requiring a PIN, blocking copy/paste to unmanaged apps, and remote wipe of just that app's corporate data, at the application level. It works even on a device that is not enrolled in MDM at all, which is exactly why it is central to BYOD scenarios.
flashcards.detail: Because app protection policy enforcement does not require device enrollment, it is the standard answer whenever a scenario needs to protect corporate data on a personal device the organization does not otherwise manage.

flashcards.back: An app configuration policy pushes predefined settings into a managed app, such as a default server URL or a disabled feature flag, at install or launch time, removing the need for a user to manually configure the app themselves after installation.
flashcards.detail: App configuration policies can target either managed devices (MDM-based) or managed apps regardless of enrollment (MAM-based), matching whichever app protection model the target population uses.

flashcards.front: Conditional Access grant control: require approved client app / app protection policy
flashcards.back: The require approved client app grant control only allows sign-in from a Microsoft-approved app, like Outlook or Teams, capable of enforcing Intune app protection. The require app protection policy grant control goes further, also requiring that a compliant app protection policy is actually applied to that app.
flashcards.detail: These two controls are what let an organization allow mail access from a personal, unenrolled phone while still blocking a generic, unmanaged mail client from ever connecting to the same mailbox.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Cloud PKI for Microsoft Intune
flashcards.back: Cloud PKI is a cloud-hosted certificate authority built into Intune that issues and manages certificates for device and user authentication, such as Wi-Fi, VPN, or app authentication, without standing up and maintaining an on-premises certificate authority or NDES infrastructure.
flashcards.detail: Cloud PKI eliminates the need for the on-premises Network Device Enrollment Service (NDES) and its connector that a traditional Intune certificate connector deployment previously required.

flashcards.back: Remote Help is an Intune-integrated app that lets a help desk technician take control of, or simply view, a managed user's remote device screen to assist with troubleshooting, with the session's permissions and role eligibility, like full control versus view only, governed by Entra ID role-based access control.
flashcards.detail: Remote Help works against both Entra ID joined and hybrid Entra joined Intune-managed devices, and requires the technician and the end user both be signed in with appropriately licensed accounts.

flashcards.front: Automating Intune with the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK
flashcards.back: Nearly every Intune object, including configuration profiles, compliance policies, app assignments, and device actions, is exposed through the Microsoft Graph API, and the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK provides cmdlets to script bulk creation, updates, and reporting against those objects instead of clicking through the Intune admin center one object at a time.
flashcards.detail: Scripted, repeatable configuration through Graph is also what backs most third-party Intune backup, migration, and configuration-as-code tooling, since the admin center UI itself has no built-in export/import for most policy types.

flashcards.front: Custom compliance policies using a detection script
flashcards.back: A custom compliance policy runs an administrator-supplied PowerShell detection script on the device and compares its JSON output against rules defined in the policy, such as a specific registry value or installed software version, extending compliance checks beyond Intune's built-in, template-based settings.
flashcards.detail: The detection script only reports data back to Intune for evaluation; it does not remediate anything itself, unlike a proactive remediation, which pairs a detection script with a separate remediation script.

flashcards.back: A proactive remediation packages a detection script and a remediation script together, running on a schedule against assigned devices. The detection script identifies a problem, and only if it reports one does the remediation script run automatically to fix it, without waiting for a user to report the issue.
flashcards.detail: Proactive remediations run under the SYSTEM account by default, which is why they can fix issues, like a corrupted registry key or a stopped service, that a standard end user account would not have rights to touch directly.

flashcards.back: Endpoint analytics measures device and user experience signals, including startup performance (boot and sign-in time breakdowns), application reliability, and resource performance, surfacing a device or fleet-wide score so IT can spot and prioritize experience problems proactively rather than waiting for help desk tickets.
flashcards.detail: Startup performance scoring breaks down exactly which phase, like a specific slow-starting driver or app, is dragging out boot time, which is what turns a vague slow-computer complaint into an actionable fix.

flashcards.back: An alert rule monitors a specific Intune signal, such as the failure rate of a deployed configuration profile or Autopatch deployment failures, against a configurable threshold, and notifies designated recipients automatically when that threshold is crossed, instead of requiring an admin to manually check dashboards.
flashcards.detail: Alert rules can be scoped with severity levels and specific notification recipients, letting a narrow team be paged only for the categories of failure that are actually their responsibility.

flashcards.back: Microsoft Security Copilot integrates with Intune through purpose-built agents that use natural-language prompts and generative AI to help an administrator investigate policy conflicts, summarize device or app issues, and get guided remediation suggestions, directly within the Intune admin center workflow.
flashcards.detail: These agents are meant to accelerate diagnosis and reduce time spent manually correlating logs and settings across many devices; they surface AI-assisted recommendations, but an administrator still reviews and approves any resulting configuration change.

flashcards.back: Shows provisioning progress during Windows Autopilot and blocks a user from reaching the desktop until required apps and configuration profiles finish installing, so the device is fully ready on first login instead of continuing to configure itself in the background.
flashcards.detail: ESP settings can be scoped separately for the out-of-box experience and for every subsequent sign-in, which matters for the different Windows Autopilot deployment profile types.

flashcards.back: The end-user-facing app (Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, macOS) where someone enrolls their own device, installs company-published apps, and checks their device's compliance status without contacting IT.
flashcards.detail: This is the client-side counterpart to compliance policy settings and actions for noncompliance — it's where a user actually sees why their device is flagged and what to fix.

flashcards.back: A VPN gateway solution managed through Intune that gives managed iOS/iPadOS and Android devices per-app or full-device access to on-premises resources, without a separate third-party VPN client or infrastructure.
flashcards.detail: Microsoft Tunnel is typically paired with app protection policies (MAM) vs mobile device management scenarios where a device may be unmanaged but a specific app still needs a secure tunnel.

flashcards.back: Wipes a Windows device back to a business-ready state — reapplying Autopilot provisioning and Intune policies — while keeping the device's Entra ID/Intune enrollment, so it doesn't need to go through Windows Autopilot device preparation vs classic Autopilot from scratch.
flashcards.detail: This is the fast option for reissuing a device to a new employee or recovering a misconfigured one, since it skips the enrollment step entirely rather than repeating it.

flashcards.back: Removing a specific installed quality update from a device that regressed after it, distinct from Safeguard holds on feature updates, which instead prevent a device from ever receiving that update in the first place.
flashcards.detail: A safeguard hold is proactive prevention before an update lands; a rollback is reactive cleanup after it already did and caused a problem.

flashcards.back: A device category is a label an end user can be prompted to choose during enrollment, or that an admin assigns afterward, used mainly for reporting, dynamic group membership, and targeting policy to devices grouped by purpose, such as 'Kiosk' or 'Executive.' A scope tag instead limits which admins can see and manage an object; the two serve different jobs and can both be applied to the same device at once.
flashcards.detail: Device categories can be surfaced as a required choice during Autopilot or standard enrollment, but changing a device's category after enrollment does not retroactively move it into a dynamic group built on that category until the group's membership is re-evaluated.

flashcards.front: Group Tag and dynamic device group targeting for Autopilot
flashcards.back: A Group Tag is a free-text attribute set on an Autopilot device registration, often during hardware vendor reservation, that a dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group can filter on, automatically placing newly registered hardware into the correct group and, through that group's assignment, the correct Autopilot deployment profile with no manual per-device assignment.
flashcards.detail: Dynamic group membership evaluation is not instantaneous, so a freshly registered device can sit briefly outside its intended group, which is why Microsoft recommends registering hardware and setting its Group Tag well before the device is due to ship.

flashcards.back: A feature update deployment profile pins a targeted group of devices to a specific target Windows version, such as forcing everyone onto 23H2 regardless of what their update ring's feature deferral would otherwise allow, and can stage that rollout gradually. It complements, rather than replaces, an update ring's separate quality-update deferral settings.
flashcards.detail: A feature update deployment profile can override an update ring's feature deferral in either direction, holding a device back from a newer version or pushing it forward faster, so having both assigned to the same device is a common source of confusion about which version actually lands.

flashcards.back: A driver update policy lets Intune manage driver and firmware updates distributed through Windows Update for Business independently of quality and feature updates, letting an admin choose to approve all drivers automatically or review and approve them individually before a targeted group of devices installs them.
flashcards.detail: Driver updates can be deferred or approved per driver, which matters because a bad OEM driver update, unlike a bad cumulative update, cannot always be resolved by a simple safeguard hold and may need to be blocked at the driver-policy level directly.

flashcards.back: An expedited update deployment lets an administrator push an urgent, already-released quality update to a targeted group of devices immediately, bypassing that group's normal update ring deferral and active-hours settings, for scenarios like a zero-day vulnerability that cannot wait for the next scheduled deployment wave.
flashcards.detail: Expediting is meant for narrow, urgent situations on a limited device count; because it can force an install and restart outside a user's normal active hours, using it broadly defeats the purpose of having deferral rings in the first place.

flashcards.back: Tenant attach uploads Configuration Manager device and collection data into the Intune admin center so an admin can see ConfigMgr-managed devices and run a limited set of remote actions, like an app install or a device sync, directly from the cloud console, without moving any co-management workload to Intune or fully enrolling the device.
flashcards.detail: Tenant attach is purely a visibility and remote-action bridge; it does not make Intune policy-authoritative for anything, which is the key distinction from actually shifting a co-management workload slider to Intune.

flashcards.front: Azure Virtual Desktop vs Windows 365 vs physical endpoints
flashcards.back: Azure Virtual Desktop hosts multi-session or personal virtual desktops on infrastructure the organization configures and scales itself in Azure, billed for consumed compute. Windows 365 is a fixed-price, per-user Cloud PC with dedicated, always-on infrastructure Microsoft manages behind the scenes. Both differ from a physical endpoint, a locally running device that is enrolled and managed through Intune the same way regardless of which management tasks apply.
flashcards.detail: A Cloud PC and a physical endpoint both show up as ordinary managed devices in Intune and can receive the same compliance policies and configuration profiles, so a scenario testing which management approach applies often hinges on licensing and infrastructure model, not on what Intune itself can configure.

flashcards.front: Dynamic vs assigned (static) Microsoft Entra ID groups for Intune targeting
flashcards.back: An assigned group requires an admin to manually add or remove each member, giving exact, deliberate control. A dynamic group instead evaluates a membership rule, such as device OS, model, or a Group Tag, and automatically adds or removes members as their attributes change, which is what lets new Autopilot hardware or a re-tagged device land in the right policy target with no manual step.
flashcards.detail: Dynamic group membership evaluation can lag by minutes, so a policy that must apply the instant a device is provisioned, such as during the Enrollment Status Page, is safer targeted through an assigned group or a Group Tag set before shipping rather than a rule evaluated after the fact.

flashcards.back: Windows Hello for Business replaces password sign-in with a PIN or biometric, face or fingerprint, that unlocks a cryptographic key pair or certificate stored on the device's TPM, providing phishing-resistant authentication that never transmits a shared secret over the network, and it is deployed and configured through an Intune device configuration or settings catalog profile.
flashcards.detail: Because the credential is bound to the specific device's TPM, a Windows Hello for Business PIN set up on one machine cannot be used to sign in on another; a user must enroll it separately on each device they use.

flashcards.back: An Intune endpoint security firewall policy configures the built-in Windows Defender Firewall's profiles, domain, private, and public, including default inbound/outbound actions and specific port or app rules, letting an admin enforce consistent network-level blocking without relying on a third-party firewall management tool.
flashcards.detail: Firewall policy settings are evaluated per network profile, so a laptop can correctly enforce a strict public-profile rule set at a coffee shop while applying a more permissive rule set on the trusted corporate network, without any separate policy switch.

flashcards.back: Windows LAPS, configured through an Intune endpoint security or settings catalog policy, automatically randomizes and periodically rotates a device's local administrator account password and backs the current password up to Microsoft Entra ID or on-premises AD, so a help desk admin can retrieve it when needed instead of every device sharing one static local admin credential.
flashcards.detail: Because each device gets its own randomized password, compromising the local admin credential on one machine no longer gives an attacker a password that also works on every other device in the fleet, closing off a classic lateral-movement path.

flashcards.front: Win32 app detection rules vs requirement rules
flashcards.back: A detection rule tells Intune how to determine whether a Win32 app is already successfully installed, such as checking for a file, registry key, or MSI product code, and is mandatory before Intune will report install status. A requirement rule instead gates whether the app is even attempted on a device at all, based on prerequisites like minimum OS version, architecture, or free disk space.
flashcards.detail: Skipping a detection rule is not allowed for a Win32 app; without one Intune has no way to confirm success, so it will keep reporting the install as pending or failing even after the installer genuinely completed.

flashcards.back: A supersedence relationship lets a newer Win32 app version automatically upgrade or replace an older deployed version on target devices, optionally uninstalling the old one first. A dependency instead declares that a different app, such as a runtime, must be installed before this app can install, and Intune installs that dependency automatically as part of the deployment.
flashcards.detail: Dependencies can chain, but a circular dependency between two apps is not allowed and will cause a deployment error, so app packaging needs a strict, one-directional dependency order.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Store app (new) replacing Microsoft Store for Business
flashcards.back: Microsoft has retired the Microsoft Store for Business and Education private store; new Microsoft Store app deployments in Intune now source apps directly from the public Microsoft Store using the modern Microsoft Store app (new) type, which supports the same required and available assignment intents without needing a separate business store front end.
flashcards.detail: Existing line-of-business apps that were side-loaded through the old Store for Business flow needed a migration plan, since simply leaving them in place after retirement does not carry forward new app updates the same way.

flashcards.front: Wipe vs Retire vs Fresh Start remote actions
flashcards.back: Wipe resets a device to factory settings, removing all data, apps, and settings, and can optionally keep it enrolled for reprovisioning. Retire removes only company data, apps, and management from the device while leaving personal data and the OS intact, typically used for BYOD offboarding. Fresh Start reinstalls a clean copy of Windows while optionally keeping user data and Intune enrollment, chiefly to strip out unwanted pre-installed OEM software.
flashcards.detail: Retire is the correct choice for a personal device enrolled through app protection or light MDM, since Wipe would destroy the user's own personal data that the organization has no right to remove.

flashcards.back: Intune provides built-in operational reports, near real-time and per-policy or per-device status, organizational reports, larger exportable datasets like device compliance trends, and a Data Warehouse/Microsoft Graph data export that can feed Power BI or Log Analytics for custom, long-term, or cross-tenant analysis beyond what the admin center's built-in views show.
flashcards.detail: Organizational reports are generated asynchronously and can take time to build for a large tenant, which is why they are the right choice for a large historical export rather than an immediate one-off status check.

flashcards.front: Conditional Access policies and Intune-aware grant controls
flashcards.back: A Conditional Access policy pairs a set of conditions, such as user, app, location, or device platform, with a grant control that decides what is required before access is allowed. Two grant controls specifically read Intune signals: the Conditional Access grant control: require device to be marked compliant checks the signing-in device's own compliance status, while the Conditional Access grant control: require approved client app / app protection policy checks that the client app itself is Microsoft-approved and, optionally, that a compliant app protection policy is actually applied to it.
flashcards.detail: A single Conditional Access policy can combine several grant controls with either a 'require all selected controls' or 'require one of the selected controls' setting, which is what lets one policy accommodate both a fully enrolled corporate laptop and an unenrolled personal phone running an approved, protected app.

flashcards.front: macOS and Android Enterprise device management in Intune
flashcards.back: Intune manages non-Windows platforms through their own native enrollment mechanisms layered under the same policy engine used for Windows: macOS enrolls through Apple's Automated Device Enrollment or user-initiated Company Portal app enrollment, while Android Enterprise offers a fully managed corporate-owned mode or a work profile mode that keeps a separate, IT-managed container alongside personal apps on a personal device. Enrollment restrictions: platform vs device limit still governs which of these platforms is even allowed to enroll in the first place.
flashcards.detail: Android Enterprise's work profile mode is the closest Android analogue to an app protection policy on an unenrolled device — both keep corporate data in an isolated, wipeable container without touching everything else on a personal device, though a work profile does still require MDM enrollment while an app protection policy does not.

flashcards.back: A kiosk configuration profile locks a device into running one app (single-app kiosk) or a curated small set of apps (multi-app kiosk), signing in as a designated local or Microsoft Entra ID account with the Start menu, taskbar, and most other Windows UI hidden from the end user. This is exactly the shared-device pattern Windows Autopilot deployment profile types anticipates when it notes that a self-deploying profile needing no user interaction is commonly used for kiosks or shared devices, since the kiosk configuration takes over immediately after that unattended provisioning finishes.
flashcards.detail: Multi-app kiosk mode still enforces AppLocker-style restrictions in the background even though it shows a friendlier, Start-menu-like tile launcher than a rigid single-app kiosk does, so an app that isn't explicitly allow-listed still won't launch even from that friendlier launcher.

flashcards.back: A device's ownership property, corporate or personal, set at enrollment, shapes what the Company Portal app shows the user and which remote action Intune permits an admin to take on it. On a corporate-owned device, Wipe vs Retire vs Fresh Start remote actions include resetting the device entirely back to factory settings for reissue or decommission, while on a personal device, Retire is the action that actually respects the organization's rights, removing only corporate data, apps, and management.
flashcards.detail: Ownership is usually set automatically by the enrollment method used, such as Autopilot for corporate-owned or self-service Company Portal enrollment for personal, but it can also be corrected manually in the Intune console if a device was enrolled through the wrong path and shows the wrong ownership type.

flashcards.back: Delivery Optimization is a Windows peer-to-peer content-sharing technology that lets devices download Windows Update for Business update ring content, Windows Autopatch payloads, and Win32 or Microsoft Store apps from nearby peers on the same network or the internet, instead of pulling every byte individually from Microsoft, reducing WAN bandwidth consumption during large rollouts.
flashcards.detail: Delivery Optimization is configured through its own settings catalog settings, with modes ranging from HTTP-only (peering disabled) to full internet peering across NAT boundaries; a branch office with limited WAN bandwidth typically restricts peering to the local network group instead of the internet-wide group.

flashcards.front: Offline domain join (ODJ) for hybrid Autopilot
flashcards.back: The Intune Connector for Active Directory can also generate an offline domain join (ODJ) blob that lets a hybrid Microsoft Entra joined Autopilot device complete its on-premises computer object creation without needing live network line-of-sight to a domain controller during the out-of-box experience.
flashcards.detail: Without ODJ, a hybrid join Autopilot device must reach a domain controller directly during OOBE — exactly the line-of-sight problem a split-tunnel VPN that only routes specific corporate traffic can create until a user manually connects first.

flashcards.back: An APNs certificate is an Apple-issued certificate that a tenant uploads to Intune to establish trust with Apple's push notification service, and it is a hard prerequisite for managing any iOS/iPadOS or macOS device, including Automated Device Enrollment — without a valid, unexpired APNs certificate, Intune cannot push MDM commands to Apple devices at all.
flashcards.detail: An APNs certificate must be renewed annually with the same Apple ID that originally created it; letting it expire doesn't just block new enrollments, it also immediately breaks management of every already-enrolled Apple device in the tenant.

flashcards.back: An administrative unit is a Microsoft Entra ID container that scopes a delegated admin's role, such as User Administrator, to only the users, groups, or devices placed inside that unit, letting a regional team manage its own directory objects without seeing or touching the rest of the tenant.
flashcards.detail: An administrative unit delegates directory-level administration in Entra ID itself; it is a different layer from scope tags, which instead limit what an Intune role can see and manage among Intune objects like policies, apps, and devices.

flashcards.back: A VPN profile or Wi-Fi profile, deployed as its own device configuration or settings catalog profile type, pushes connection settings, such as server address, authentication method, and SSID, to managed devices automatically, and commonly pairs with a certificate profile sourced from Microsoft Cloud PKI or SCEP so the device authenticates with a certificate instead of a typed password.
flashcards.detail: Deploying the certificate profile and the VPN or Wi-Fi profile to the same device group is what actually lets authentication succeed silently; the connection profile alone, with no matching certificate delivered to the device, fails at the authentication step.

flashcards.back: An Intune endpoint security Antivirus policy configures Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings such as cloud-delivered protection level, real-time protection, scheduled and quick scan behavior, and scan exclusions, independent of the separate attack surface reduction (ASR) rules and firewall policy nodes in endpoint security.
flashcards.detail: Raising cloud-delivered protection to its highest blocking level trades a small amount of scan latency, while a file is checked against the cloud, for faster coverage of brand-new malware that a signature-only, offline-only configuration would miss.

flashcards.front: Account protection policy (local user group membership)
flashcards.back: An Intune endpoint security Account protection policy can enforce which users or groups belong to a device's local groups, such as the local Administrators group, continuously reapplying the defined membership so anyone added outside of policy is automatically removed the next time the policy evaluates.
flashcards.detail: This is a different control from Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS): Account protection decides who is allowed to be a local administrator at all, while LAPS instead randomizes and rotates the password of whichever local administrator account already exists.

flashcards.back: An iOS/iPadOS or Android compliance policy can require that a device not be jailbroken or rooted, automatically failing compliance for any device Intune detects has had its OS-level restrictions bypassed, since a jailbroken or rooted device can no longer be trusted to enforce the rest of the policy's own settings.
flashcards.detail: This setting pairs naturally with compliance policy settings and actions for noncompliance: a device that fails jailbreak detection can trigger the same escalating noncompliance actions, up to losing Conditional Access-gated access, as any other failed compliance rule.

flashcards.front: Apple VPP (Apple Business Manager) app licensing
flashcards.back: Apple Volume Purchase Program licensing, managed through an Apple Business Manager token added to Intune, lets an organization buy and assign App Store app licenses in bulk, either to a device (device licensing, no Apple ID needed on the device) or to a specific user's Apple ID (user licensing), then deploy and reclaim those licenses through Intune the same way as any other required or available app assignment.
flashcards.detail: Device licensing is generally preferred for shared or kiosk-style corporate iPads since it needs no personal Apple ID on the device at all, while user licensing is tied to one person's Apple ID and moves with them if they get a new device.

flashcards.back: Managed Google Play is the enterprise storefront Intune connects to for distributing public, private, and web apps to Android Enterprise devices, whether fully managed corporate-owned or work profile mode, letting an admin approve and assign apps from the same Google Play catalog employees already know without a personal Google account being required on a corporate-owned device.
flashcards.detail: A Managed Google Play connection, established once per tenant from the Intune admin center, is a prerequisite for any Android Enterprise app deployment, the same way an Apple VPP (Apple Business Manager) app licensing token is a prerequisite for bulk-licensed Apple App Store deployments.

flashcards.front: Win32 app install context (system vs user)
flashcards.back: A Win32 app package can be set to install in the system context, running once for the whole device under SYSTEM regardless of who signs in, or the user context, running separately for each signed-in user; choosing the wrong context for how the installer itself behaves is a common cause of an app that Intune reports as successfully installed but that a specific user never actually sees.
flashcards.detail: An installer built to write Start menu shortcuts and registry keys per-user will silently fail to register for anyone if it's deployed in system context, even though the install itself, and the detection rule vs requirement rules check behind it, both report success.

flashcards.back: Collect diagnostics gathers a managed Windows device's logs, event data, and configuration state into a package an admin can download from the Intune admin center, without needing physical access to the device or walking an end user through manually exporting logs over a support call.
flashcards.detail: This remote action is read-only and makes no change to the device itself, unlike Wipe, Retire, or a remote restart, so running it carries no risk of disrupting a user who is actively working on the machine.

flashcards.back: Remote lock immediately locks a managed device's screen, requiring its PIN, password, or Windows Hello for Business credential to unlock again, giving an admin a fast way to secure a lost or misplaced device without wiping any data off it.
flashcards.detail: Remote lock is a lighter, reversible response than Wipe vs Retire vs Fresh Start remote actions; it buys time to confirm a device is truly lost before committing to a destructive action that cannot be undone.

flashcards.back: Windows Update for Business reports is a built-in Azure Monitor workbook, backed by a Log Analytics workspace connected to the tenant, that shows feature and quality update deployment status, compliance deadlines, and failure details across enrolled devices in one consolidated update-focused view, separate from Intune's general-purpose operational and organizational reports.
flashcards.detail: Because it runs on Log Analytics, Windows Update for Business reports can be queried directly with Kusto Query Language (KQL) for custom views, rather than being limited to the Intune admin center's built-in report layout.

flashcards.back: The Troubleshooting + support blade in the Intune admin center lets an admin look up one specific user or device and see exactly which policies, apps, and profiles are assigned, their individual deployment status, and recent enrollment or sync history, turning a vague 'my policy isn't applying' ticket into a per-object status check instead of a tenant-wide guess.
flashcards.detail: This is usually the fastest first stop for a one-user, one-device complaint, while an alert rule or an organizational report is better suited to a pattern affecting many devices at once rather than troubleshooting a single case.

flashcards.back: Tamper protection, enabled through an Intune endpoint security Antivirus policy or security baseline, locks core Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings, such as real-time protection and cloud-delivered protection, against being changed locally, including by a signed-in local administrator, so a compromised or careless admin session cannot quietly disable antivirus protection on the device.
flashcards.detail: Because tamper protection blocks changes made directly on the device itself, an admin who genuinely needs to adjust a protected setting must do so centrally through the Intune policy, not by editing the setting locally on the endpoint.

flashcards.back: An indicators policy, managed in the Microsoft Defender portal and scoped to onboarded devices, lets an admin explicitly allow or block specific files, certificates, IP addresses, or URLs/domains by their exact identifier, overriding Defender's normal detection logic for just that one indicator across every onboarded device.
flashcards.detail: Indicators are useful for two opposite situations at once: blocking a specific malicious hash security research has identified, or allowing a legitimate internal tool that antivirus heuristics keep misidentifying as suspicious.

flashcards.front: BitLocker encryption type: used space only vs full disk
flashcards.back: An Intune encryption profile's BitLocker settings let an admin choose used space only encryption, which encrypts only the sectors currently holding data and finishes faster, or full disk encryption, which also encrypts every empty sector and takes longer but leaves no unencrypted free space that could later retain recoverable traces of deleted data.
flashcards.detail: Used space only is the common default for a brand-new device with no prior unencrypted data ever written to it, while full disk encryption is the safer choice for a drive that was previously used unencrypted before BitLocker was turned on.

flashcards.front: Device control policy for removable storage
flashcards.back: An Intune endpoint security device control policy, part of the attack surface reduction category, can block or restrict removable storage such as USB drives, by device class or by specific hardware ID, preventing data exfiltration or malware introduction through removable media without having to physically disable USB ports.
flashcards.detail: Device control can be scoped narrowly, such as allowing only specific, approved USB device IDs while blocking every other removable drive, rather than an all-or-nothing block on every USB port.

flashcards.back: Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate and protect cached domain credentials and NTLM hashes in a secured enclave the operating system itself cannot access, so even malware running with local administrator rights cannot extract reusable credentials from an infected device.
flashcards.detail: Credential Guard addresses the same credential-theft-from-LSASS problem that attack surface reduction (ASR) rules can also target, but through hardware-backed isolation instead of behavior-based blocking.

flashcards.back: An LOB app uploads a single .msi, .appx, or similar installer file directly to Intune with no packaging step, but supports only basic install/uninstall behavior and a built-in detection method tied to the package itself. A Win32 app instead requires converting the install source into the .intunewin format first, in exchange for full support for custom detection rules, requirement rules, dependencies, and supersedence.
flashcards.detail: An app that only needs a simple, single-file install with no dependency chain or version-upgrade logic can stay an LOB app and skip the .intunewin packaging step entirely; one that needs supersedence or a prerequisite runtime must be packaged as a Win32 app instead.

flashcards.back: The Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool converts an application's setup folder into the .intunewin format Intune requires for a Win32 app upload, encrypting the package in transit and at rest in Intune so the installer's contents are not exposed in plain form.
flashcards.detail: This packaging step happens once per app version, outside of the Intune admin center itself, before the resulting .intunewin file is ever uploaded as a new Win32 app or a new version through supersedence.

flashcards.back: An app protection policy's settings are organized into three groups: data protection, which controls things like copy/paste and backup behavior; access requirements, which controls PIN and biometric prompts; and conditional launch, which blocks or wipes the app's data if a condition is met, such as the app being launched on a jailbroken device or after too many failed PIN attempts.
flashcards.detail: Conditional launch is the enforcement layer that actually acts on a violation, such as triggering a selective wipe of corporate data, rather than simply configuring a preventive control like data protection or access requirements.

flashcards.front: Microsoft 365 Apps deployment and update channels
flashcards.back: Intune can deploy Microsoft 365 Apps (the Click-to-Run suite including Word, Excel, and Outlook) as its own app type, letting an admin pick which update channel, such as Current Channel, Monthly Enterprise Channel, or Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel, controls how often that installation receives new features and fixes.
flashcards.detail: Monthly Enterprise Channel is the common middle-ground choice, delivering new features once a month on a predictable date rather than the more frequent Current Channel cadence or the twice-a-year Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel.

flashcards.back: MAM-WE is the scenario where an app protection policy enforces data controls on a managed app even though the device itself was never enrolled in MDM at all; the app only needs the user to be registered with Microsoft Entra ID, which is what makes it possible on a personal device the organization never took management of.
flashcards.detail: MAM-WE is the specific term for the exact capability behind app protection policies (MAM) vs mobile device management: enforcement that reaches the app's data without ever reaching the rest of the unenrolled device.

flashcards.back: Microsoft Intune Suite is a licensed add-on bundle that unlocks premium Intune capabilities beyond the base license, such as Advanced Endpoint Analytics, Enterprise App Management, premium certificate issuance through Cloud PKI, and remote help features, for organizations that need deeper capability than what the base Intune plan includes.
flashcards.detail: Features bundled in the Intune Suite are sold together rather than piecemeal, so licensing the suite is the way to unlock several premium capabilities, such as expanded endpoint analytics, at once rather than enabling each individually.

flashcards.back: A policy set groups multiple apps, configuration profiles, compliance policies, and other assignable items into one single object that can be assigned to a group all at once, instead of an admin individually assigning each item every time a new group of users or devices needs the same combination.
flashcards.detail: Policy sets simplify onboarding a new department or location that needs the identical bundle of apps and policies every other similar group already has, since the whole bundle is assigned in one step rather than reassigning each piece separately.

flashcards.back: Windows 365 Boot lets a user sign in to a physical Windows device directly into their Cloud PC at the login screen instead of the local desktop. Windows 365 Switch lets a user already signed in locally move back and forth between their local desktop and their Cloud PC from within the same session, similar to switching between virtual desktops.
flashcards.detail: Boot is about how a session starts, landing straight in the Cloud PC from the lock screen, while Switch is about moving between a local and cloud session once already signed in; a device can support both features at once.

flashcards.back: Autopilot for existing devices converts a device that is already in service, such as one previously imaged with Configuration Manager, into an Autopilot-managed device using a provisioning package built with Windows Configuration Designer, registering it for a self-deploying or user-driven profile without needing the OEM to have registered its hardware hash in advance.
flashcards.detail: This is the path to adopt Autopilot for a fleet of devices already deployed years ago, rather than only for brand-new hardware a reseller or OEM registers at the point of sale.

flashcards.front: Corporate device identifiers (IMEI/serial number allow list)
flashcards.back: A corporate device identifiers list lets an admin upload a set of IMEI numbers or serial numbers to mark specific hardware as corporate-owned at enrollment, independent of the platform and device-limit restrictions enrollment restrictions otherwise apply, which instead cap enrollment by OS type or by how many devices one user can add.
flashcards.detail: Marking a device as corporate-owned through its identifier matters because device ownership controls which Company Portal experience and remote actions, like Wipe vs Retire vs Fresh Start remote actions, an admin is allowed to use against it later.

questions.question: A company is setting up unattended digital-signage kiosks that must provision themselves with zero end-user interaction, using only the device's own identity to authenticate during Autopilot enrollment. Which Autopilot profile type fits?
options: A user-driven Autopilot profile
A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile
A self-deploying Autopilot profile
Windows Autopilot device preparation configured for hybrid Entra join
questions.explanation: A self-deploying profile authenticates using the device's own identity and needs no end-user sign-in at all, which is exactly what an unattended kiosk requires. A user-driven profile needs a user to sign in, a white glove profile still finishes with a short user-facing phase, and device preparation currently targets Entra join only, not this unattended self-authenticating pattern.

questions.question: An IT partner completes lengthy driver installation and app packaging on new laptops before shipping them to remote new hires, who then only need to enter their own name and Wi-Fi credentials to finish setup. Which Autopilot profile type was used?
options: A user-driven profile
A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile
A self-deploying profile
Windows Autopilot device preparation in device-driven mode
questions.explanation: A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile is specifically for letting a partner or IT complete the time-consuming steps in advance, leaving only a short final phase for the end user. A plain user-driven profile has the end user complete the entire process themselves, and a self-deploying profile needs no user interaction at all.

questions.question: An administrator wants to enroll a fleet of devices into Windows Autopatch so Microsoft manages their update deployment rings automatically. What must be true about a device before it can be added?
options: The device must already be enrolled and managed by Intune, and appropriately licensed for Autopatch
The device must be hybrid Entra joined; Microsoft Entra joined devices aren't eligible for Autopatch enrollment
The device must be under Configuration Manager co-management with no Intune enrollment
The device requires no enrollment or licensing to join Autopatch
questions.explanation: Autopatch requires a device to already be enrolled and managed by Intune and covered by an appropriate license, such as Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5, before it can be added; readiness checks confirm this. It is not restricted to hybrid join only, and it does not work on unenrolled, unmanaged devices.

questions.question: A team wants to reduce how often end users are prompted to reboot for monthly security updates, without giving up periodic full cumulative updates entirely. What does deploying Windows Hotpatch achieve?
options: It removes the need for a reboot after this specific update, though the following month's update goes back to requiring one
It still requires a reboot each month, but only for out-of-band emergency security fixes
It's specifically for driver updates, and rolls out separately from monthly security updates
It applies a subset of security fixes in memory without the usual reboot, while periodic baseline cumulative updates are still needed occasionally
questions.explanation: Hotpatching applies eligible security fixes in memory without the reboot a normal cumulative update requires, though the device still periodically needs a baseline cumulative update since not every fix can be applied this way. It reduces reboot frequency rather than eliminating reboots permanently, and it is specifically about security updates, not drivers.

questions.question: A warehouse runs three shifts a day with far more total employees than the number who are ever logged in to a shared kiosk PC at the same time. The company wants Cloud PCs for these workers without licensing one dedicated Cloud PC per named employee. Which licensing model fits?
options: Windows 365 Enterprise, licensing one Cloud PC per named employee
Windows 365 Frontline, sized to the maximum number of concurrent users rather than the total number of named users
No Windows 365 license is required for shared kiosk scenarios
Windows Autopatch licensing applied to the shared kiosk PCs
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Frontline licenses a smaller shared pool of Cloud PCs sized to the maximum number of concurrent connections, which fits shift workers who never all log in at once, far more cost-effectively than licensing every named employee under Enterprise. Autopatch is an update-management service, not a Cloud PC licensing model.

questions.question: An update ring is configured with a 0-day quality update deferral but a 60-day feature update deferral. What happens to devices in that ring?
options: The lower of the two configured deferral values applies to both feature and quality updates on this ring
Quality updates wait for the 60-day feature deferral period to elapse before they're delivered to the ring
Feature and quality update deferrals are independent, so the ring receives quality updates immediately while staying on its current feature version for up to 60 more days
The update ring controls feature updates only; quality updates are instead managed through a separate compliance policy
questions.explanation: Feature and quality update deferrals are configured and applied independently within the same update ring, so this ring gets near-immediate monthly quality updates while remaining on its current Windows feature version for up to 60 additional days. The two deferral types do not have to match, and an update ring controls both, not just one.

questions.question: In a co-managed, hybrid Entra joined environment, an administrator moves only the Device Configuration workload slider to Intune, leaving every other workload slider set to Configuration Manager. What is the result?
options: Only the Device Configuration workload is now managed by Intune; Configuration Manager remains installed and authoritative for every workload whose slider was not moved
The Configuration Manager client is automatically uninstalled from the device
All workloads immediately shift to Intune once any single slider is moved
Compliance policy management also silently shifts to Intune as a side effect
questions.explanation: Each co-management workload slider is independent: moving only Device Configuration to Intune makes Intune authoritative for that one workload while Configuration Manager continues managing every other workload, and its client remains installed. Moving one slider has no automatic effect on any other workload's authority.

questions.question: A set of devices is already domain-joined to on-premises Active Directory and hybrid Microsoft Entra joined, but they are not yet enrolled in Intune. The company wants them to pick up MDM enrollment automatically with minimal manual work per device. What should be configured?
options: A pre-provisioned (white glove) Autopilot profile
A bulk enrollment provisioning package built with Windows Configuration Designer
Manual self-enrollment through Settings on each device
Automatic MDM enrollment via Group Policy, since the devices are already hybrid Entra joined and domain-joined
questions.explanation: GPO-based automatic MDM enrollment is built exactly for already domain-joined, hybrid Entra joined devices that simply need to pick up MDM enrollment with no fresh provisioning process. Autopilot and provisioning packages are for provisioning new or reset devices from scratch, and manual per-device enrollment does not scale.

questions.question: A specific model of laptop is not being offered the latest Windows feature update through its update ring, even though every configured deferral period has already elapsed. What is the most likely explanation?
options: An administrator must have misconfigured the ring's deferral period, since every device in the ring should otherwise receive the update together
A safeguard hold that Microsoft applied automatically after detecting a known compatibility issue on that device or hardware model; an admin can review and choose to override it in Intune
The device has failed its compliance policy, and noncompliant devices are automatically excluded from feature update rollout
The feature update package requires a specific application to be uninstalled and reinstalled first, which hasn't happened yet on this device
questions.explanation: A safeguard hold is applied automatically by Microsoft when a known compatibility issue is detected for a device or hardware/driver combination, blocking the specific feature update until Microsoft lifts it or an admin explicitly overrides the hold in Intune. It is unrelated to deferral misconfiguration or compliance policy status.
questions.whyTested: This is one of the exam's favorite 'don't blame your own configuration' traps: it's built so that admin misconfiguration is the intuitive first guess, testing whether you recognize a safeguard hold as something Microsoft deliberately triggers on purpose rather than jumping to 'something must be wrong with the ring.'

questions.question: A brand-new Microsoft 365 tenant has Intune licenses assigned to every user, but every enrollment attempt fails tenant-wide with no device able to enroll at all. What should be checked first?
options: Whether app protection policies have been created
Whether an enrollment restriction is blocking every platform
Whether MDM authority has been set for the tenant, since Intune cannot enroll any device without it
Whether a scope tag has been applied to the default policy set
questions.explanation: Without MDM authority configured for the tenant, Intune cannot enroll any device at all, regardless of licensing, which makes it the first thing to check for a tenant-wide enrollment failure. Enrollment restrictions, scope tags, and app protection policies would cause narrower, not universal, enrollment failures.

questions.question: A company wants only members of its managers group to be able to enroll iOS devices, while every other user is limited to three devices of any platform. How should this be configured?
options: Create a higher-priority platform restriction and device limit restriction scoped to the managers group, leaving the lower-priority default restriction to apply to everyone else
Edit the default enrollment restriction directly, lowering its priority so it applies only to the managers group instead
Use a compliance policy to block iOS enrollment for non-managers
Use a Conditional Access policy to prevent iOS enrollment
questions.explanation: Enrollment restrictions can be created as additional, higher-priority restrictions scoped to a specific group, evaluated ahead of the built-in default restriction that applies to everyone else, exactly matching this scenario. Compliance policies and Conditional Access govern post-enrollment access, not whether enrollment itself is allowed.

questions.question: A newly released CSP-backed setting is not available in any of the existing built-in device configuration profile templates, including Endpoint Protection. The administrator needs to configure it for managed Windows devices right away. What should they use?
options: The Endpoint Protection template regardless, since a template's available settings periodically expand automatically behind the scenes
Wait for Microsoft to add the setting to an existing template in a future Intune service update before configuring anything
A PowerShell script deployed manually to every device instead of any Intune profile, since Intune has no way to reach settings this new
The settings catalog, since it exposes newly available CSP-backed settings individually as they become available
questions.explanation: The settings catalog surfaces essentially every available CSP-backed setting individually and is kept current as new settings become available, unlike some older templates that are no longer actively updated. There is no need to wait for a template update or resort to manual scripting.

questions.question: A desktop is already joined to on-premises Active Directory via Group Policy and needs to also register with Microsoft Entra ID so it can be enrolled in Intune and evaluated by Conditional Access. What device state should it end up in?
options: Microsoft Entra registered only, since registration alone is sufficient for Intune enrollment and Conditional Access evaluation
Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined, since it is already domain-joined to on-premises AD and also needs to register with Entra ID
Microsoft Entra joined, dropping the on-premises AD account entirely once Entra ID registration completes
No Entra ID relationship is needed, since on-premises Group Policy already provides equivalent device management
questions.explanation: Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined describes exactly this device: joined to on-premises AD and also registered with Microsoft Entra ID, enabling Intune enrollment and Conditional Access evaluation. Entra registered alone is typically for personal/BYOD devices, and Entra joined alone implies no existing on-premises AD account.

questions.question: Employees already hold Microsoft 365 E3 licenses, which include Intune for device management. The company now wants to provision Windows 365 Cloud PCs for some of those same employees. What additional step is required purely for licensing?
options: Nothing extra is required, since Intune management already covers Windows 365
Every employee must be upgraded to Microsoft 365 E5, since only E5 includes the Windows 365 entitlement bundled in
A separate Windows 365 Cloud PC license (Enterprise or Frontline) must be assigned, since Windows 365 is licensed separately from Intune device management
Enterprise Mobility + Security alone is sufficient to provision Cloud PCs
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Cloud PC requires its own separate per-user license layered on top of whatever license already provides Intune management; M365 E3 alone does not include a Cloud PC entitlement. An E5 upgrade is not required specifically for Windows 365, and EMS alone does not include Cloud PC licensing either.

questions.question: A global organization wants its regional helpdesk teams to see and manage only the devices and policies belonging to their own region within the same Intune tenant, without splitting into separate tenants. What should be configured?
options: Assign a scope tag matching each region to the relevant devices and policies, and scope each regional admin's role assignment to that same tag
Rely on Azure RBAC roles alone, since Intune has no native delegation mechanism
Create a separate administrative unit for each region in Microsoft Entra ID, since scope tags do not exist in Intune
Configure a device enrollment restriction per region instead, since restrictions can also scope which admins see which devices
questions.explanation: Scope tags applied to devices and policies, combined with role assignments scoped to those same tags, are exactly the built-in Intune mechanism for regional delegation within a single tenant. Administrative units and enrollment restrictions solve different problems, and Intune does have its own native scope-tag-based delegation.

questions.question: A hybrid Entra join Autopilot deployment is otherwise correctly configured, but every device fails during provisioning specifically at the on-premises domain-join step. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Autopilot deployment profile itself is misconfigured
A device enrollment restriction is blocking the devices
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync is not running
The Intune Connector for Active Directory is missing, unhealthy, or not installed, since it performs the on-premises computer object creation step during hybrid join Autopilot
questions.explanation: The Intune Connector for Active Directory bridges cloud-based Autopilot provisioning with the on-premises AD domain-join step for hybrid Entra join, and its absence or ill health causes failures specifically at that stage even when the rest of the configuration is correct. A profile misconfiguration or enrollment restriction would typically fail earlier or differently.

questions.question: A configuration profile is assigned to the All Devices group, but the administrator only wants it to actually apply to devices running Windows 11, not older Windows 10 devices also in that group. What should be added to the assignment?
options: A separate group containing only Windows 11 devices, replacing the All Devices assignment entirely
An assignment filter on the profile's assignment, scoped to match only Windows 11 devices
Filters are unnecessary, since group assignment alone always narrows by OS version automatically
Nothing; Intune resolves this kind of mixed-OS conflict automatically with no configuration needed
questions.explanation: An assignment filter layers on top of an existing group assignment, so a device must be in the assigned group and match the filter (here, Windows 11) to actually receive the profile, without needing to build and maintain a separate group. Group assignment alone does not narrow by OS version.

questions.question: A device fails its compliance policy this morning. The policy's noncompliance actions include a 5-day grace period before Conditional Access blocks access. What happens to the device's access today?
options: Access is blocked within the hour, since Conditional Access re-evaluates compliance signals hourly regardless of the configured grace period
The device isn't marked noncompliant at all until the grace period elapses without remediation
The device is marked noncompliant immediately, but Conditional Access continues to allow access until the grace period expires
Compliance policies only support a grace period on mobile platforms, not for a Windows endpoint like this one
questions.explanation: The device is flagged noncompliant right away, but the escalating noncompliance actions mean Conditional Access does not actually block access until the configured grace period elapses without remediation. Grace periods are a standard, configurable part of a compliance policy's noncompliance actions.

questions.question: A Conditional Access policy requires devices to be marked as compliant. A user signs in from a personal, noncompliant phone and also from a compliant, corporate-issued laptop. What happens?
options: Access is evaluated per device: the compliant laptop is granted access under that grant control while the same user is blocked on the noncompliant phone
The user is blocked everywhere, since one of their devices is noncompliant
The user is granted access everywhere, since at least one of their devices is compliant
The grant control only evaluates the user's account, not any specific device
questions.explanation: The require device to be marked as compliant grant control is evaluated against the specific device used for that sign-in, not the user's overall device fleet, so the compliant laptop passes while the noncompliant phone is blocked. It is explicitly device-bound rather than user-bound.
questions.whyTested: MD-102 repeatedly tests whether you track a Conditional Access grant control at the device level or the user level, because that single detail flips the right answer between 'blocked everywhere' and 'blocked only on this one device' — a distinction real admins get wrong constantly when troubleshooting an access ticket.

questions.question: A security team wants a device's Intune compliance status to automatically reflect its real-time threat risk as assessed by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, so a compromised device quickly loses Conditional Access-gated access. What should be configured?
options: A security baseline assigned to the device with no other change
An attack surface reduction rule in audit mode
A BitLocker recovery key escrow policy
Onboard the devices to Defender for Endpoint through an Intune onboarding profile, then add a device risk level requirement to the compliance policy
questions.explanation: Onboarding devices to Defender for Endpoint connects their risk signals to Intune, and adding a maximum allowed device risk level to the compliance policy is what makes an actively compromised device automatically fail compliance. Security baselines, ASR audit mode, and BitLocker key escrow do not by themselves feed compliance status this way.

questions.question: A security baseline was assigned to a device group a year ago. Microsoft has since released a newer baseline version with additional recommended settings, but the managed devices show no change in enforced settings. Why?
options: Assigned baselines update their settings automatically with no admin action
The baseline profile instance must be explicitly moved to the newer baseline version before the updated settings take effect
A brand new baseline profile must be created from an empty template, since existing instances are locked to the version they were first assigned
Baseline settings only change if the device group's membership itself changes, independent of the profile's baseline version
questions.explanation: Security baselines are versioned, and picking up a newer version's changes requires an administrator to explicitly move the existing profile instance to that new version; it does not happen automatically. The instance itself does not need to be rebuilt from scratch to do this, though.

questions.question: A help desk team needs to be able to look up a locked-out user's BitLocker recovery key themselves during a support call, without the user having written the key down anywhere. What should be configured in the encryption profile?
options: Disable BitLocker recovery key backup entirely
Store the recovery key only locally on the affected device
Store the recovery key in Microsoft Entra ID, so a help desk technician can look it up there during the call
Require the user to generate and manage their own recovery key manually
