questions.explanation: Configuring the encryption profile to escrow the BitLocker recovery key to Microsoft Entra ID lets an authorized help desk technician retrieve it there during a support call, with no dependency on the end user having saved it themselves. Storing it only locally on the encrypted device would not be retrievable by anyone if the user cannot access it.

questions.question: Developers need to run a specific, IT-approved internal tool that requires administrator rights to install, but the security team does not want to add developers to the local Administrators group. What should be configured?
options: An Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule scoped to that specific approved application
Add every developer to the local Administrators group temporarily
Disable User Account Control on developer devices
Require developers to call the help desk every time they need to install the tool
questions.explanation: Endpoint Privilege Management lets a standard user elevate one specific, approved application without granting them full local administrator rights, which is exactly the least-privilege outcome this scenario needs. Adding developers to local Administrators or disabling UAC would grant far broader rights than required.

questions.question: A company wants its standard productivity suite installed automatically on every managed device with no user action needed, while a specialized utility remains optional and available only for users who choose to install it from the Company Portal. How should these two apps be assigned?
options: Assign both apps as Required
Assign the productivity suite as Required and the utility as Available
Assign both apps as Available
Assign both apps as Uninstall
questions.explanation: A Required assignment installs an app automatically with no user action, matching the productivity suite's needs, while an Available assignment lists an app in Company Portal for optional, user-initiated install, matching the utility. Assigning both the same way would either force-install the optional utility or fail to auto-install the mandatory suite.

questions.question: Employees use their own personal, unenrolled phones to check corporate email in Outlook. The company wants to require a PIN and block copying corporate data into unmanaged apps, without enrolling any of these personal devices in MDM. What should be deployed?
options: A device compliance policy targeting the personal phones, since compliance policies can enforce PIN and copy-paste restrictions the same way app protection does
A device configuration profile requiring MDM enrollment first, since PIN and copy-paste controls are configuration-profile settings, not app-level ones
A security baseline applied to the Outlook app, since baselines can be scoped to individual applications instead of only devices
An app protection (MAM) policy targeting the Outlook app, since it enforces data controls without requiring device enrollment
questions.explanation: App protection policies enforce controls like PIN requirements and copy/paste restrictions at the application level and work even on devices that are not MDM-enrolled, which is exactly what this BYOD scenario needs. Compliance policies, configuration profiles, and security baselines all require or target MDM-managed devices.
questions.whyTested: Exams stack four plausible-sounding controls — compliance policy, configuration profile, security baseline, app protection policy — that all sound like they could enforce a PIN, specifically to test whether you know which single one operates below the MDM-enrollment line, since that's the detail that actually makes or breaks a BYOD deployment.

questions.question: An administrator wants a managed line-of-business app to automatically receive its correct backend server URL the first time each user launches it, without the user having to type it in manually. What should be created?
options: An app configuration policy targeting that app with the required key-value settings
An app protection policy with a PIN requirement
A device compliance policy referencing the server URL
A security baseline scoped to that app
questions.explanation: An app configuration policy pushes predefined settings, such as a default server URL, into a managed app at install or launch time, removing the need for manual user configuration. App protection policies, compliance policies, and security baselines do not push app-specific configuration values like this.

questions.question: A company wants to allow corporate mail access from any Microsoft-approved app capable of enforcing Intune app protection, such as Outlook, while blocking a generic, unmanaged third-party mail client from connecting to the same mailbox at all. Which Conditional Access grant control achieves this?
options: Require device to be marked as compliant
Block all access from mobile devices
Require approved client app
Require hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device
questions.explanation: The require approved client app grant control only allows sign-in from a Microsoft-approved app capable of enforcing app protection, letting Outlook through while blocking a generic unmanaged mail client. Requiring device compliance or hybrid join would apply to full device state, not specifically which client app is being used to connect.

questions.question: A company needs to issue Wi-Fi authentication certificates to managed devices but does not want to stand up or maintain an on-premises certificate authority or NDES server. What should they deploy?
options: A traditional Intune SCEP certificate profile pointed at an on-premises NDES server
Microsoft Cloud PKI for Intune, issuing certificates from its cloud-hosted certificate authority
Self-signed certificates manually installed on each device
A SCEP profile with no certificate authority configured at all
questions.explanation: Cloud PKI provides a cloud-hosted certificate authority built into Intune, issuing device and user authentication certificates like Wi-Fi without any on-premises CA or NDES infrastructure. A traditional SCEP profile still depends on an on-premises NDES server, which the scenario explicitly wants to avoid.

questions.question: A help desk team needs to remotely view or take control of a managed employee's device screen for troubleshooting, with different technicians granted either full control or view-only rights depending on their role. What should be deployed and configured?
options: A generic third-party remote desktop tool with a shared password
An app protection policy targeting the help desk technicians
A device configuration profile enabling Remote Desktop Protocol
Remote Help, with technicians assigned an Entra ID role that grants the needed permission level
questions.explanation: Remote Help is the Intune-integrated tool purpose-built for this, with session permissions like full control versus view-only governed by Entra ID role-based access control assigned to each technician. Generic RDP or third-party tools do not integrate with Intune-managed device context and role-based permission levels this way.

questions.question: An administrator needs to create several dozen similar configuration profiles across many Intune device groups and wants to avoid manually clicking through the admin center for each one. What should they use?
options: The Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK to script the object creation through Microsoft Graph
Configuration Manager, since Intune has no scripting or automation surface at all
Group Policy Objects applied to Entra joined devices
Manual creation through the Intune admin center only, since bulk scripting is not supported
questions.explanation: Nearly every Intune object is exposed through Microsoft Graph, and the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK provides cmdlets to script bulk creation instead of manual, one-at-a-time admin center work. Group Policy does not apply to cloud-managed configuration profiles, and Intune's admin center itself has no bulk-create feature for this.

questions.question: An administrator needs to check for a specific registry value that Intune's built-in, template-based compliance settings have no option to evaluate at all. What should they configure?
options: A built-in device restriction compliance setting
A security baseline profile
A custom compliance policy using a detection script that reports the registry value, evaluated against rules defined in the policy
An app configuration policy targeting the registry
questions.explanation: A custom compliance policy runs an administrator-supplied detection script and evaluates its reported data against rules in the policy, extending compliance checks beyond what built-in templates cover, including arbitrary registry values. Security baselines and app configuration policies do not provide this kind of custom, scriptable compliance check.
questions.whyTested: The exam likes offering several built-in-sounding constructs, like a security baseline or app configuration policy, as distractors for a genuinely custom capability, testing whether you remember that only a custom compliance policy runs your own arbitrary detection script instead of a fixed set of vendor-defined settings.

questions.question: A recurring issue causes a critical background service to stop on some devices. The team wants it automatically detected and restarted before users notice or file a help desk ticket, with no manual intervention. What should be deployed?
options: A custom compliance policy alone, with no remediation script
A proactive remediation pairing a detection script for the stopped service with a remediation script that restarts it
An Intune alert rule with no associated script
Endpoint analytics resource performance scoring alone
questions.explanation: A proactive remediation runs a detection script on a schedule and, only if it reports the problem, automatically runs a paired remediation script to fix it without waiting for a user report. A custom compliance policy only reports status and does not remediate, and alert rules and endpoint analytics surface signals rather than taking automatic fix actions.

questions.question: Users across the fleet report slow boot times, but IT cannot tell whether the delay comes from a specific driver, a startup app, or something else. Which built-in Intune capability breaks down exactly where the boot-time delay is coming from?
options: Windows Update for Business reporting
A custom compliance policy detection script
An Intune alert rule threshold
Endpoint analytics startup performance, which breaks down boot time by phase, including slow-starting drivers
questions.explanation: Endpoint analytics startup performance specifically breaks boot time down by phase, identifying which driver, app, or component is responsible, turning a vague slow-boot complaint into an actionable fix. Update reporting, alert rules, and compliance scripts do not provide this kind of phase-level startup breakdown.

questions.question: An administrator wants AI-assisted, natural-language help investigating a policy conflict directly within the Intune admin center, rather than manually correlating logs and settings across many devices. What should they use?
options: A Security Copilot agent integrated into Intune
A proactive remediation script
Endpoint analytics resource performance scoring
An Intune alert rule with no natural-language capability
questions.explanation: Security Copilot agents integrated into Intune use natural-language prompts and generative AI to help investigate issues like policy conflicts and suggest guided remediation directly in the admin center workflow. Proactive remediations, endpoint analytics, and alert rules are useful signals but provide no natural-language, AI-assisted investigation of this kind.

questions.question: In a Windows Update for Business update ring, feature update deferral and quality update deferral are configured and applied independently of each other.
questions.explanation: The two deferral types are separate settings within the same ring, so a device can defer feature updates for months while still receiving monthly quality updates on a much shorter deferral.

questions.question: A device must already be enrolled and managed by Intune before it can be added to Windows Autopatch.
questions.explanation: Autopatch enrollment requires the device to already be Intune-managed and appropriately licensed; it does not manage unenrolled, unmanaged devices.

questions.question: A self-deploying Autopilot profile requires an end user to sign in with their own Microsoft Entra ID account during provisioning.
questions.explanation: A self-deploying profile needs no end-user sign-in at all; the device authenticates using its own identity, which is why it fits unattended kiosk-style scenarios.

questions.question: Moving the Device Configuration workload slider to Intune in a co-managed environment immediately uninstalls the Configuration Manager client from the device.
questions.explanation: Moving a workload slider only changes which management tool is authoritative for that specific workload; the Configuration Manager client remains installed and continues managing every workload whose slider was not moved.

questions.question: The Intune settings catalog exposes CSP-backed settings individually, searchable and combinable into one custom profile, rather than grouping them into fixed templates.
questions.explanation: That is the defining difference between the settings catalog and the older, template-based device configuration profiles, which bundle related settings into purpose-built templates instead.

questions.question: Device enrollment restrictions are evaluated in priority order, similar to Conditional Access policies, with the most specific assigned restriction taking precedence.
questions.explanation: Enrollment restrictions support multiple assigned restrictions evaluated in priority order, with a built-in default restriction acting as the fallback for anyone not covered by a higher-priority one.

questions.question: A Microsoft 365 E3 license that includes Intune automatically also grants a Windows 365 Cloud PC to every licensed user.
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Cloud PC requires its own separate per-user license, Enterprise or Frontline, layered on top of whatever license already provides Intune management; it is not bundled automatically with M365 E3.

questions.question: As soon as a device is marked noncompliant, Conditional Access immediately blocks its access with no grace period possible.
questions.explanation: A compliance policy's noncompliance actions can include a configurable grace period, during which the device is flagged noncompliant but Conditional Access still allows access until that period elapses.

questions.question: An Intune encryption profile can be configured to store a device's BitLocker recovery key in Microsoft Entra ID for help desk retrieval.
questions.explanation: Escrowing the recovery key to Microsoft Entra ID is a standard encryption profile option, letting a help desk technician retrieve it during a self-service or assisted recovery call.

questions.question: Endpoint Privilege Management permanently adds the end user to the local Administrators group once an elevation rule is configured for them.
questions.explanation: EPM elevates only the specific, approved application defined in the rule; the user is never added to the local Administrators group and does not gain broader standing administrator rights.

questions.question: An Intune app protection (MAM) policy requires the target device to be enrolled in mobile device management before its controls take effect.
questions.explanation: App protection policies enforce data controls at the application level and work even on devices that are not MDM-enrolled at all, which is exactly why they are central to BYOD scenarios.

questions.question: Microsoft Cloud PKI for Intune removes the need to deploy and maintain an on-premises Network Device Enrollment Service (NDES) server.
questions.explanation: Cloud PKI is a cloud-hosted certificate authority built into Intune, eliminating the on-premises NDES server and connector a traditional Intune certificate connector deployment previously required.

questions.question: Intune proactive remediation scripts run under the SYSTEM account on the device by default.
questions.explanation: Running under SYSTEM by default is exactly why proactive remediations can fix issues, like a corrupted registry key or a stopped service, that a standard end user account would not have rights to touch directly.

questions.question: A custom compliance policy's detection script both evaluates the device and automatically remediates any problem it finds.
questions.explanation: A custom compliance detection script only reports data back to Intune for evaluation against the policy's rules; it does not remediate anything itself. Automatic fixing is what a proactive remediation's separate remediation script does.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Windows Autopilot profile types? (Choose two.)
options: A self-deploying profile authenticates the device itself and needs no end-user sign-in
A user-driven profile requires no end-user interaction at all
A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile lets IT or a partner complete most of the provisioning steps before the device ships to the end user
Self-deploying profiles work on any device regardless of TPM support
questions.explanation: A self-deploying profile needs no user sign-in because the device authenticates itself, and a white glove profile is specifically for pre-completing most of the setup before shipping. A user-driven profile does require end-user interaction, and self-deploying profiles specifically require TPM 2.0 support, not just any device.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Windows Autopatch and Windows Hotpatch? (Choose two.)
options: Hotpatch updates always eliminate the need for any reboot, permanently
Windows Autopatch organizes enrolled devices into deployment rings and manages update rollout schedules automatically
Hotpatch is unrelated to security updates and only applies to driver updates
A device must already be Intune-managed and appropriately licensed before it can be enrolled in Autopatch
questions.explanation: Autopatch automatically organizes devices into deployment rings and manages rollout schedules, and it requires a device to already be Intune-managed and licensed before enrollment. Hotpatch reduces reboot frequency rather than eliminating reboots permanently, since periodic baseline cumulative updates are still needed, and it specifically applies to security updates, not drivers.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Microsoft Entra device join states? (Choose two.)
options: A Microsoft Entra joined device is owned by the organization and has no on-premises AD account
A Microsoft Entra registered device receives the same full device-level compliance policy enforcement as a joined device
Hybrid Entra join requires no on-premises Active Directory infrastructure at all
A hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device is joined to on-premises AD and also registered with Entra ID
questions.explanation: A Microsoft Entra joined device has no on-premises AD account, while a hybrid Entra joined device has both an on-premises AD account and Entra ID registration. A registered BYOD device is generally managed through mobile application management rather than full device-level compliance, and hybrid join by definition depends on on-premises AD infrastructure.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Intune compliance policies and Conditional Access integration? (Choose two.)
options: Marking a device noncompliant automatically deletes it from Intune
The require device to be marked as compliant grant control evaluates the specific device's compliance status at sign-in
A device's compliance status can incorporate a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint risk level once the device is onboarded
Compliance policies cannot include any Conditional Access-related actions at all
questions.explanation: The compliant-device grant control checks the specific device used at sign-in, and a compliance policy can require a maximum Defender for Endpoint risk level once onboarding is configured. Marking a device noncompliant does not delete it from Intune, and compliance policies routinely feed Conditional Access through this exact grant control.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Intune app protection policies and app configuration policies? (Choose two.)
options: App protection policies can enforce data controls on a managed app without the device being enrolled in MDM
App configuration policies can push default settings into a managed app at install or launch time
App protection policies always require full device enrollment first
App configuration policies can only target apps deployed through Configuration Manager
questions.explanation: App protection policies work at the application level and specifically do not require MDM enrollment, and app configuration policies push settings like a default server URL into a managed app automatically. App protection policies do not require full device enrollment, and app configuration policies are not limited to Configuration Manager-deployed apps.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Microsoft Cloud PKI and Remote Help in Intune? (Choose two.)
options: Cloud PKI requires an on-premises NDES server to issue any certificate
Remote Help can only be used against devices that are hybrid Entra joined
Remote Help session permissions, like full control versus view only, are governed by Entra ID role-based access control
Cloud PKI can issue certificates for device and user authentication scenarios like Wi-Fi or VPN
questions.explanation: Remote Help session permission levels are governed by Entra ID role-based access control, and Cloud PKI issues certificates for scenarios like Wi-Fi and VPN authentication directly from its cloud-hosted CA. Cloud PKI specifically removes the need for an on-premises NDES server, and Remote Help works against both Entra joined and hybrid Entra joined devices, not only hybrid.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about proactive remediations and custom compliance scripts? (Choose two.)
options: A custom compliance policy's detection script can automatically remediate the condition it detects
A proactive remediation runs a detection script and, only if it reports a problem, automatically runs a paired remediation script
Custom compliance detection scripts cannot report anything beyond a simple pass/fail with no additional data
Proactive remediation scripts run under the SYSTEM account on the device by default
questions.explanation: A proactive remediation only runs its remediation script when the paired detection script reports a problem, and both scripts run under the SYSTEM account by default. A custom compliance detection script only reports status for evaluation and never remediates anything itself, and it can report structured data beyond a simple pass/fail.

questions.question: An administrator wants managed devices automatically grouped by their purpose, such as 'Kiosk' or 'Executive,' for reporting and dynamic group targeting, without changing which admins are allowed to see or manage those devices. What should be used?
options: A scope tag applied to each device
A device category, either admin-assigned or chosen by the user during enrollment
An assignment filter based on device manufacturer
A compliance policy naming each purpose
questions.explanation: A device category is exactly the label meant for grouping devices by purpose for reporting and dynamic group targeting, and it is independent of admin visibility. A scope tag instead controls which admins can see and manage an object, not how devices are grouped by purpose.

questions.question: New laptops are registered for Autopilot with a Group Tag matching their business unit before they ship. The company wants each laptop to automatically land in the correct Autopilot deployment profile with no manual per-device assignment. What should be configured?
options: A static assigned group that an admin updates manually for each new device
A dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group with a membership rule based on the Group Tag, assigned to the matching deployment profile
A scope tag matching each business unit
An assignment filter with no group assignment at all
questions.explanation: A dynamic group with a membership rule on the Group Tag attribute automatically places newly registered hardware into the right group, and through that group's assignment, the right deployment profile, with no manual work. A static group would require exactly the manual per-device work the scenario wants to avoid, and an assignment filter narrows an existing group assignment rather than replacing it.

questions.question: A pilot group's update ring defers feature updates for 180 days, but the administrator needs that same pilot group to receive Windows 11 23H2 immediately for early testing, without changing the ring's deferral setting. What should be configured?
options: A feature update deployment profile targeting the pilot group and pinned to 23H2, which can override the ring's feature deferral
A driver update policy targeting 23H2
An expedited quality update targeting the pilot group
Nothing; feature update deferral cannot be overridden once set
questions.explanation: A feature update deployment profile pins targeted devices to a specific Windows version and can override an update ring's feature deferral in either direction, letting the pilot group move to 23H2 immediately without touching the ring itself. A driver update policy and expedited quality updates govern different update types entirely.

questions.question: An organization keeps most workloads on Configuration Manager but wants its help desk to view ConfigMgr-managed devices and trigger a quick app install from the Intune admin center, without moving any co-management workload to Intune or re-enrolling any device. What should be configured?
options: Move every co-management workload slider to Intune
Tenant attach, uploading Configuration Manager device data to the Intune admin center for visibility and a limited set of remote actions
Enroll every device fresh into Intune using Autopilot
Deploy Microsoft Tunnel to the ConfigMgr devices
questions.explanation: Tenant attach is built exactly for this: it surfaces ConfigMgr device and collection data in the Intune admin center and allows a limited set of remote actions like an app install, without shifting any workload's authority or re-enrolling anything. Moving workload sliders or re-enrolling devices would change management authority, which the scenario explicitly wants to avoid.

questions.question: A company wants a fixed monthly cost per user for a dedicated, always-on virtual desktop, with the underlying infrastructure fully managed behind the scenes rather than something the company scales and configures itself in Azure. Which solution fits, and how is it managed once running?
options: Azure Virtual Desktop, since it is billed for consumed compute and configured directly by the company
Windows 365, since it provides a fixed-price, dedicated Cloud PC with Microsoft managing the underlying infrastructure; the Cloud PC is then managed through Intune like any other device
A physical endpoint provisioned through Autopilot, since only physical hardware can be Intune-managed
Neither option can be managed through Intune once deployed
questions.explanation: Windows 365 specifically offers a fixed per-user price with Microsoft managing the underlying infrastructure, unlike Azure Virtual Desktop's consumption-based, company-configured model, and the resulting Cloud PC shows up as an ordinary Intune-managed device. Both AVD session hosts and Windows 365 Cloud PCs can be managed through Intune, so management is not limited to physical hardware.

questions.question: A company wants to eliminate password-based sign-in on managed Windows laptops in favor of a PIN or biometric unlock backed by a device-bound cryptographic key, with no shared secret transmitted over the network. What should be deployed through Intune?
options: A device compliance policy requiring a minimum password length
Windows Hello for Business, configured through a device configuration or settings catalog profile
Endpoint Privilege Management with an elevation rule
A Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business is the feature that replaces password sign-in with a PIN or biometric that unlocks a TPM-bound key pair, providing phishing-resistant authentication with no shared secret sent over the network, and it is deployed via device configuration. A compliance policy or Conditional Access control device access requirements rather than replacing the sign-in credential itself.

questions.question: A security review finds that every device in the fleet shares the same static local administrator password, creating a lateral-movement risk if one device is compromised. What should be deployed through Intune to fix this?
options: A single new shared local administrator password rolled out to every device
Windows LAPS, so each device gets its own randomized, periodically rotated local administrator password backed up to Microsoft Entra ID
Endpoint Privilege Management applied to the local administrator account itself
A BitLocker recovery key rotation policy
questions.explanation: Windows LAPS randomizes and rotates each device's local administrator password independently and escrows the current value to Microsoft Entra ID for retrieval, which directly eliminates the shared-password lateral-movement risk. Rolling out one new shared password would only recreate the same problem, and BitLocker key rotation addresses disk encryption, not the local admin account.

questions.question: An administrator packages a Win32 app in Intune but leaves the detection rule unconfigured. What is the result when the app is deployed?
options: Intune assumes the install succeeded automatically since no detection rule was defined
Intune blocks upload of any Win32 app package that lacks a detection rule
A detection rule is mandatory for a Win32 app; without one, Intune cannot confirm the install and keeps reporting it as pending or failed even after it actually completed
The app's requirement rule automatically doubles as its detection rule
questions.explanation: A detection rule is how Intune determines whether a Win32 app installed successfully, and it is required; without one, Intune has no way to confirm success and will keep reporting an ambiguous or failed status even if the install genuinely worked. A requirement rule serves a different purpose, gating whether the app is attempted at all, and cannot substitute for detection.

questions.question: An admin needs a newly packaged Win32 app version to automatically replace an older deployed version on target devices, uninstalling the old version first. Which Win32 app relationship should be configured?
options: A dependency relationship pointing from the new version to the old version
A supersedence relationship, with the new version configured to uninstall the old version before installing
An assignment filter targeting only devices with the old version installed
A detection rule referencing the old version's registry key
questions.explanation: A supersedence relationship is exactly what lets a newer Win32 app version automatically upgrade or replace an older deployed version, optionally uninstalling the old one first. A dependency instead declares a prerequisite app that must install before this one, which is not what an in-place version upgrade needs.

questions.question: A user leaves the company and returns their personally owned phone, which was enrolled only through an app protection policy for corporate email access, with no full MDM enrollment. What remote action correctly removes corporate data and access without touching the user's personal data?
options: Wipe, resetting the device to factory settings
Retire, removing company data, apps, and management while leaving personal data and the OS intact
Fresh Start, reinstalling a clean copy of the OS
Autopilot Reset, reapplying provisioning
questions.explanation: Retire is built for exactly this offboarding scenario: it removes company data, apps, and management from the device while leaving the user's personal data and OS untouched, appropriate for a personally owned device. Wipe would destroy personal data the organization has no right to remove, and Fresh Start and Autopilot Reset are provisioning-focused actions for organization-owned Windows devices, not personal phone offboarding.

questions.question: A Windows driver update policy in Intune can be configured to require administrator review and approval of individual drivers before they are installed on targeted devices, rather than approving every driver automatically.
questions.explanation: Driver update policies support both an automatic-approval mode and a mode where an admin reviews and approves individual drivers before rollout, giving control over potentially risky OEM driver updates.

questions.question: A dynamic Microsoft Entra ID group updates its membership automatically based on a rule, such as device model or a Group Tag, while an assigned group requires an admin to manually add or remove each member.
questions.explanation: That is the core difference between the two group types: dynamic membership is rule-evaluated and automatic, while assigned (static) group membership is manually maintained by an admin.

questions.question: An Intune endpoint security firewall policy can enforce different rule sets for a device's domain, private, and public network profiles, applying the appropriate rules automatically as the device's network changes.
questions.explanation: Firewall policy settings are evaluated per Windows Defender Firewall network profile, so a device correctly applies a stricter public-profile rule set on an untrusted network and a more permissive domain/private rule set on the trusted corporate network without manual switching.

questions.question: Intune organizational reports and the Data Warehouse/Microsoft Graph data export are generated synchronously and appear instantly, making them the right tool for checking a single device's real-time policy status.
questions.explanation: Organizational reports and the Data Warehouse export are generated asynchronously and can take time to build for a large tenant, so they suit large historical or cross-tenant analysis; a real-time, per-device status check is better answered by Intune's operational reports.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about feature update deployment profiles and expedited quality updates in Intune? (Choose two.)
options: A feature update deployment profile can pin a targeted group of devices to a specific Windows version regardless of that group's update ring feature deferral
Expediting a quality update is intended for broad, routine monthly rollout across the entire fleet
Expediting a quality update can bypass a targeted group's normal deferral and active hours for an urgent fix
Feature update deployment profiles and update rings cannot both be assigned to the same device
questions.explanation: A feature update deployment profile pins devices to a specific version independent of the ring's deferral, and expediting is built to push an urgent fix past normal deferral and active hours. Expediting is meant for narrow, urgent scenarios rather than routine broad rollout, and a device can have both a feature update deployment profile and an update ring assigned at once.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Win32 app management and the modern Microsoft Store app in Intune? (Choose two.)
options: A circular dependency between two Win32 apps is supported and resolved automatically by Intune
A Win32 app dependency causes Intune to automatically install the prerequisite app as part of the deployment
The Microsoft Store for Business and Education private store has been retired in favor of the Microsoft Store app (new), which sources apps from the public store
The Microsoft Store app (new) type does not support required or available assignment intents
questions.explanation: A Win32 app dependency causes Intune to automatically install the declared prerequisite app first, and the old Microsoft Store for Business/Education private store has been retired in favor of the Microsoft Store app (new) sourcing directly from the public store. Intune does not support or auto-resolve a circular dependency between two apps, and the Microsoft Store app (new) type does support the same required/available assignment intents as other app types.

questions.question: Which built-in Windows Autopatch deployment ring is intended to receive updates last, after the Test, First, and Fast rings have already validated them?
options: Broad
Test
First
Fast
questions.explanation: Autopatch's four default rings are Test, First, Fast, and Broad, applied in that order, with Broad — holding the bulk of the fleet — receiving updates last, after the earlier, smaller rings have already validated them.

questions.question: A device is enrolled in Autopatch and is eligible for Hotpatch, but it hasn't installed a baseline cumulative update in over four months, skipping several opportunities to do so. What is likely to happen the next time a hotpatch is released?
options: The device isn't eligible to receive that hotpatch until it installs a baseline update first, since hotpatching applies a delta on top of a sufficiently recent baseline
The hotpatch installs normally regardless of how outdated the device's baseline update is
Autopatch permanently revokes the device's Hotpatch eligibility after one missed baseline
The device is removed from Autopatch entirely for being out of compliance
questions.explanation: A hotpatch is a delta applied on top of a recent enough baseline cumulative update; a device too far behind on baseline updates isn't eligible for that hotpatch until it catches up. Missing baseline updates doesn't install a hotpatch anyway, doesn't permanently revoke eligibility, and doesn't remove the device from Autopatch outright.

questions.question: A device is hybrid Entra joined, domain-joined, and already has the Configuration Manager client installed, but is not yet enrolled in Intune. GPO-based automatic MDM enrollment is configured tenant-wide. An administrator also enables co-management on this same device. What is the resulting Intune enrollment state, and which workloads does Intune control?
options: The device becomes Intune-enrolled through automatic MDM enrollment, but Intune only becomes authoritative for the specific workloads whose co-management sliders have been moved to it — everything else stays with Configuration Manager
The device cannot be both Intune-enrolled and Configuration Manager-managed at the same time, so co-management fails until Configuration Manager is uninstalled
Intune becomes authoritative for every workload the moment enrollment completes, regardless of slider positions
GPO-based automatic enrollment is blocked on any device that already has the Configuration Manager client installed
questions.explanation: GPO-based automatic enrollment works normally on an already domain-joined, hybrid Entra joined device regardless of the Configuration Manager client, and co-management is specifically designed to let that device be both Intune-enrolled and Configuration Manager-managed at once, with each workload slider independently deciding which tool is authoritative for it.

questions.question: A reseller wants to automatically register newly purchased Windows devices for Autopilot on the customer's behalf at the point of sale, without the customer manually uploading a hardware hash file for each device after delivery. Which registration method enables this?
options: Registration via an OEM or Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) partner, tied to the device's hardware identity at the point of sale
Manually exporting each device's hardware hash with a PowerShell script after it arrives
Registering devices individually through Windows Configuration Designer after unboxing
Using a device enrollment restriction to register devices automatically
questions.explanation: OEM and CSP partner registration captures a device's hardware identity at the point of sale and registers it for Autopilot on the customer's behalf, with no post-delivery hash export needed. A PowerShell hash export and Windows Configuration Designer both require the device to already be in hand, and an enrollment restriction only limits who can enroll — it doesn't register hardware for Autopilot at all.

questions.question: A global company wants regional IT admins to manage only their own region's Intune devices and policies within one tenant, and separately wants regional HR admins to manage only their own region's Entra ID user accounts and licensing, also within that same one tenant. Which pairing of features fits each need respectively?
options: Scope tags with scoped role assignments for the regional Intune delegation; administrative units for the regional Entra ID user/license delegation
Administrative units for the regional Intune delegation; scope tags for the regional Entra ID user/license delegation
A single scope tag covering both the Intune and Entra ID objects for both teams
Separate Entra ID tenants, one per region, unified through B2B guest access
questions.explanation: Scope tags with scoped role assignments are Intune's own delegation mechanism for devices and policies, while administrative units are Entra ID's delegation mechanism for scoping user and license administration — swapping the two applies the wrong tool to each directory. A single scope tag can't reach into Entra ID user/license administration at all, and separate tenants would be a far heavier solution than delegating within one.

questions.question: A compliance policy's noncompliance actions currently only block Conditional Access access after a grace period. The security team also wants an email automatically sent to the device's user as soon as it's first marked noncompliant, before the grace period even starts counting down. What should be added to the policy?
options: An additional noncompliance action sending an email notification, configured with an action schedule of 0 days
A Conditional Access policy with an email connector
A device configuration profile with a notification setting
An app protection policy targeting the user's mailbox app
questions.explanation: A compliance policy supports multiple noncompliance actions, each with its own schedule; adding an email-notification action scheduled at 0 days fires immediately at first noncompliance, independent of the separate, longer-scheduled access-block action. Conditional Access, device configuration profiles, and app protection policies don't provide this kind of scheduled noncompliance notification at all.

questions.question: A team wants standard users to be able to install and run one specific IT-approved application that needs administrator rights, without ever granting that user standing local administrator access, and separately wants help desk to still be able to look up a fallback local admin password for that same machine during an emergency. Which pairing of features satisfies both needs without contradiction?
options: Endpoint Privilege Management for the scoped application elevation; Windows LAPS for the separate, rotated local administrator account password
Windows LAPS alone, granting the user a rotated local administrator password only when installing the approved app
Endpoint Privilege Management alone, since it also manages and rotates the local administrator account password
Adding the user to the local Administrators group, then removing them immediately after each install finishes
questions.explanation: EPM elevates just the one approved application without granting standing admin rights, and Windows LAPS independently manages a rotated local administrator account password for the genuinely needed emergency fallback — the two are complementary, addressing different problems. LAPS doesn't grant users elevated rights to run apps, EPM doesn't manage or rotate the local administrator account's password, and manually toggling group membership around each install recreates the standing-access risk the team wants to avoid, and doesn't scale.

questions.question: An LOB Win32 app has a required assignment to a device group, and depends on a separate prerequisite Win32 app that is not yet assigned to that same group. What happens when Intune tries to install the required app?
options: Intune automatically installs the declared dependency first, then installs the requiring app, without needing the prerequisite separately assigned to the group
The required app installation fails outright, since its dependency was never separately assigned
Intune skips the dependency and installs the requiring app anyway, leaving the prerequisite missing
The dependency must be manually installed by the end user before the required app will proceed
questions.explanation: A Win32 app dependency relationship causes Intune to automatically install the declared prerequisite as part of deploying the requiring app, with no separate assignment of the prerequisite needed. Installation doesn't fail or skip the dependency, and nothing about this requires manual end-user action.

questions.question: A proactive remediation's detection script correctly identifies a stopped service on affected devices, but the paired remediation script that's supposed to restart that service keeps failing specifically on devices where the service depends on a mapped network drive available only in the interactively logged-on user's context. What is the most likely cause?
options: Both scripts run under the SYSTEM account by default, which has no access to the interactive user's mapped drives unless the remediation is explicitly reconfigured to run in user context
Proactive remediation scripts can only detect problems and are never able to remediate them at all
The detection script must have a bug, since remediation scripts always inherit the exact same environment as the interactive user automatically
Remediation scripts are blocked from restarting any Windows service, regardless of execution context
questions.explanation: Proactive remediation scripts run under the SYSTEM account by default, which has no visibility into a specific interactive user's mapped drives — reconfiguring the remediation to run in the logged-on user's context is what resolves this. Remediation scripts absolutely can fix problems (that's their purpose), they don't automatically inherit the interactive user's environment, and there's no blanket restriction on restarting services from a remediation script.

questions.question: A company has many devices at a branch office with a slow, metered WAN link, and most of them need to download the same large feature update at the same time. Which Windows feature lets nearby devices share already-downloaded update content with each other instead of each one pulling the full file over the WAN link individually?
options: Delivery Optimization, configured to peer within the local network
Windows Autopatch, since it throttles download speed automatically for metered connections
A feature update deployment profile, since it controls which version each device receives
Windows Update for Business reports, since it tracks update download progress per device
questions.explanation: Delivery Optimization lets devices share already-downloaded update, Autopatch, and app content with nearby peers on the same network instead of each device pulling the full file individually from Microsoft, directly easing a congested WAN link. Autopatch manages rollout scheduling rather than peer caching, a feature update deployment profile pins a target version rather than managing bandwidth, and Windows Update for Business reports only reports on status rather than changing how content is delivered.

questions.question: An admin wants to enroll a batch of new iPads into Intune using Automated Device Enrollment, but every enrollment attempt fails immediately, and existing iPhones already managed by Intune have also just stopped receiving any MDM commands. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs) certificate has expired and needs to be renewed with the same Apple ID that created it
An enrollment restriction is blocking the iOS platform for all users
A Managed Google Play connection has not been configured for the tenant
The devices are missing a Wi-Fi configuration profile
questions.explanation: An expired APNs certificate breaks management for every already-enrolled Apple device at once and blocks all new Apple enrollment simultaneously, matching both symptoms together. An enrollment restriction would typically block only new enrollment, not already-managed devices; Managed Google Play applies to Android, not Apple; and a missing Wi-Fi profile would not affect enrollment or MDM command delivery this broadly.

questions.question: A multinational company wants its regional HR teams to manage user accounts and group memberships for only their own region's employees in Microsoft Entra ID, without granting them any ability to view or manage Intune policies at all. What should be configured?
options: A scope tag assigned to each region's user accounts
An administrative unit per region, containing that region's users and groups, with the HR team's role assignment scoped to it
An enrollment restriction limiting devices by region
A dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group per region
questions.explanation: An administrative unit scopes a delegated Entra ID role, such as User Administrator, to only the users and groups placed inside it, which is exactly the directory-level delegation this HR scenario needs with no Intune access implied. A scope tag only limits Intune object visibility, not Entra ID user administration, and enrollment restrictions and device groups govern devices, not user account management.

questions.question: A security team wants managed Windows devices to get faster protection against brand-new malware by checking suspicious files against Microsoft's cloud intelligence during a scan, accepting a small amount of added scan latency in exchange. What should be configured?
options: A higher cloud-delivered protection level in an Intune Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy
An attack surface reduction rule in block mode
A Windows Defender Firewall policy for the public network profile
A security baseline left at its default version
questions.explanation: Cloud-delivered protection level in a Defender Antivirus policy is exactly the setting that checks files against Microsoft's cloud intelligence for faster coverage of brand-new threats, at the cost of a small amount of scan latency. Attack surface reduction rules target specific exploited behaviors rather than general cloud-based scanning, firewall policy governs network traffic rather than file scanning, and a baseline left at its default version introduces no new protection on its own.

questions.question: An admin notices that a help-desk technician was added to the local Administrators group on a managed laptop outside of any approved process, and wants Intune to automatically remove anyone from that group who isn't on an approved list, every time the policy checks. What should be deployed?
options: An Account protection policy defining the approved local group membership
Windows LAPS, since it also controls who belongs to the local Administrators group
An Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule
A compliance policy requiring a minimum OS version
questions.explanation: An Account protection policy enforces a defined local group membership and automatically removes anyone added outside of it the next time the policy evaluates, which is exactly this scenario. Windows LAPS rotates the password of whichever local administrator account already exists rather than deciding group membership, EPM elevates one specific application rather than managing group membership, and a minimum OS version compliance check is unrelated to local group membership.

questions.question: A school wants to buy App Store app licenses in bulk for a cart of shared iPads, with no personal Apple ID required on any of the devices, and deploy them through Intune. What should be configured?
options: Apple VPP (Apple Business Manager) device licensing through a token added to Intune
Apple VPP user licensing tied to each student's personal Apple ID
Managed Google Play, since it supports device-based licensing with no personal account
A Win32 app dependency relationship for each app
questions.explanation: Apple VPP device licensing, enabled through an Apple Business Manager token in Intune, assigns App Store licenses directly to a device with no personal Apple ID needed, matching a shared-iPad cart exactly. User licensing ties a license to one person's Apple ID instead, Managed Google Play is the Android Enterprise app store rather than an Apple one, and a Win32 app dependency is unrelated to Apple app licensing.

questions.question: A Win32 app shows a successful install status for every targeted device in Intune, but one department reports the app's shortcut never appears on their Start menu, even though the files are present on disk. The installer is designed to register its shortcuts per signed-in user. What is the most likely cause?
options: The app was packaged to install in the system context instead of the user context the installer actually needs
The app's detection rule was left unconfigured
The affected devices are missing a required assignment filter
The app's supersedence relationship is misconfigured
questions.explanation: An installer that registers shortcuts per signed-in user needs to run in user context; deploying it in system context lets the underlying files install successfully under SYSTEM while never actually registering for any individual user, exactly matching the symptom. A missing detection rule would prevent Intune from ever reporting success at all, a missing filter would prevent the app from targeting the devices in the first place, and a supersedence misconfiguration concerns version upgrades, not per-user shortcut registration.

questions.question: A technician is troubleshooting a device remotely and wants to pull its current logs and configuration state into the Intune admin center for review, without changing anything on the device or disrupting the user currently working on it. What should they use?
options: The Collect diagnostics remote action
The Wipe remote action, configured to keep the device enrolled
A proactive remediation with no remediation script attached
The Retire remote action
questions.explanation: Collect diagnostics gathers a device's logs and configuration state into a downloadable package without making any change to the device, so it carries no risk of disrupting an active user. Wipe and Retire both remove data or management from the device, and a proactive remediation with no remediation script would only report a detection result rather than collecting full diagnostic logs.

questions.question: An employee reports their corporate laptop is missing and may have simply been left in a meeting room. The admin wants to immediately secure the device without destroying any data, in case it turns up within the hour. What should they do?
options: Use the Remote lock action, requiring the device's credential to unlock again
Use the Wipe action, keeping the device enrolled for reprovisioning
Use the Retire action, removing company data and management
Use Autopilot Reset to reapply provisioning
questions.explanation: Remote lock immediately secures the device by requiring its credential to unlock, without removing any data, making it the reversible first response while there is still a reasonable chance the device will be found. Wipe, Retire, and Autopilot Reset are all more destructive or disruptive actions appropriate once a device is confirmed lost or being reissued, not for a device that may simply be misplaced nearby.

questions.question: An admin wants a consolidated, update-specific view of feature and quality update deployment status and compliance deadlines across the fleet, and wants to be able to query that data directly with KQL for a custom view. What should they use?
options: Windows Update for Business reports, backed by a connected Log Analytics workspace
Intune's built-in operational reports
A custom compliance policy's detection script output
Endpoint analytics resource performance scoring
questions.explanation: Windows Update for Business reports is the update-focused Azure Monitor workbook backed by Log Analytics, letting an admin query update deployment data directly with KQL for custom views. Operational reports are general-purpose and don't offer KQL querying, a compliance detection script reports only what its author scripted, and endpoint analytics resource performance measures device experience rather than update deployment status.

questions.question: An offline domain join (ODJ) blob generated through the Intune Connector for Active Directory lets a hybrid Microsoft Entra joined Autopilot device complete its on-premises computer object creation without needing live line-of-sight to a domain controller during the out-of-box experience.
questions.explanation: That is exactly what ODJ provides: a pre-generated domain-join blob that removes the need for the device to reach a domain controller directly during OOBE, which is otherwise a common point of failure for hybrid join over a split-tunnel VPN.

questions.question: An iOS or Android compliance policy that includes jailbreak/root detection will mark a jailbroken or rooted device as compliant as long as every other compliance setting still passes.
questions.explanation: Jailbreak or root detection fails a device's compliance on its own, regardless of whether every other setting passes, since a jailbroken or rooted device can no longer be trusted to enforce the rest of the policy's settings.

questions.question: A Managed Google Play connection must be established once per tenant in the Intune admin center before any Android Enterprise app can be deployed to fully managed or work profile devices.
questions.explanation: Managed Google Play is the enterprise storefront Intune connects to for Android Enterprise app distribution, and that tenant-level connection is a prerequisite before any app can be approved and assigned to either fully managed or work profile devices.

questions.question: The Troubleshooting + support blade in the Intune admin center is best suited to diagnosing a pattern of failures affecting many devices at once, rather than looking up one specific user's assigned policies and status.
questions.explanation: The Troubleshooting + support blade is built for the opposite case: looking up one specific user or device to see its assigned policies, apps, and recent status, which makes it the fastest first stop for a single-user complaint. A fleet-wide pattern is better suited to an alert rule or an organizational report.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about VPN and Wi-Fi configuration profiles in Intune? (Choose two.)
options: A VPN or Wi-Fi profile commonly pairs with a certificate profile so the device authenticates without a typed password
A VPN or Wi-Fi profile automatically issues its own certificates with no separate certificate profile needed
A certificate profile delivered without a matching VPN or Wi-Fi profile is sufficient on its own for a device to connect
Microsoft Cloud PKI or a SCEP-based certificate profile can supply the certificate a VPN or Wi-Fi profile authenticates with
questions.explanation: A VPN or Wi-Fi profile commonly pairs with a certificate sourced from Cloud PKI or SCEP so the device authenticates without a typed password. A VPN or Wi-Fi profile does not issue certificates itself — it depends on a separate certificate profile — and a certificate alone with no connection profile gives the device nothing to actually connect with.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Apple VPP and Managed Google Play app deployment in Intune? (Choose two.)
options: Apple VPP device licensing assigns an App Store license directly to a device with no personal Apple ID required
Managed Google Play requires a personal Google account on every corporate-owned Android device before any app can be assigned
A Managed Google Play connection is established once per tenant and is a prerequisite for Android Enterprise app deployment
Apple VPP licensing can only be assigned to a user's personal Apple ID, never directly to a device
questions.explanation: Apple VPP device licensing assigns a license straight to a device with no personal Apple ID needed, and a Managed Google Play connection is a one-time, tenant-level prerequisite before Android Enterprise apps can be deployed at all. Managed Google Play does not require a personal Google account on a corporate-owned device, and Apple VPP does support device licensing in addition to user licensing, not user licensing exclusively.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Intune remote actions? (Choose two.)
options: Collect diagnostics gathers a device's logs and configuration state without making any change to the device itself
Remote lock permanently erases all data on the device
Remote lock is a reversible way to secure a device while its loss is still being confirmed
Collect diagnostics automatically wipes the device once logs are gathered
questions.explanation: Collect diagnostics only gathers logs and configuration state with no change to the device, and Remote lock secures a device reversibly without destroying data, buying time before a more drastic action is needed. Remote lock does not erase data — that describes Wipe — and Collect diagnostics never triggers a wipe on its own.

questions.question: An attacker gains local administrator rights on a managed Windows laptop and tries to disable Microsoft Defender Antivirus's real-time protection directly on the device to avoid detection. Which setting is specifically designed to block that local change from taking effect?
options: A higher cloud-delivered protection level in the Antivirus policy
Tamper protection, enabled through the Antivirus policy or a security baseline
An attack surface reduction rule in block mode
A device control policy restricting removable storage
questions.explanation: Tamper protection specifically locks core Defender Antivirus settings, like real-time protection, against being changed locally, even by someone with local administrator rights, blocking exactly this attack. Cloud-delivered protection level, ASR rules, and device control policy all harden the device in other ways but do not themselves prevent a local admin from disabling antivirus protection directly.

questions.question: Security researchers publish the exact file hash of a new piece of malware. The security team wants every device already onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to block that specific file the next time it appears, without waiting for a signature update. What should they configure?
options: An indicators policy in the Microsoft Defender portal blocking that specific file hash
A higher cloud-delivered protection level in the Antivirus policy
An attack surface reduction rule in audit mode
A custom compliance policy detection script checking for the file
questions.explanation: An indicators policy lets an admin block a specific file, certificate, IP address, or URL by its exact identifier across every onboarded device immediately, which is exactly this scenario. A higher cloud protection level and ASR audit mode both work on broader detection patterns rather than one named hash, and a compliance detection script only reports status without blocking anything.

questions.question: A manufacturing floor needs most USB drives blocked to prevent data walking out the door, but a small set of approved, IT-issued USB drives, identified by their specific hardware IDs, must still be allowed to work. What should be configured?
options: An attack surface reduction rule blocking removable storage entirely
A device control policy allowing only the approved hardware IDs while blocking other removable storage
A compliance policy marking devices noncompliant when a USB drive is detected
A conditional access policy blocking sign-in from any device with a USB port
questions.explanation: A device control policy can scope removable storage restrictions down to specific hardware IDs, allowing only the approved drives while blocking everything else, which an all-or-nothing ASR block cannot do. A compliance policy would only report a finding rather than block drive use, and Conditional Access governs sign-in access, not USB hardware behavior.

questions.question: An admin needs to deploy a simple single-file MSI installer that requires no dependency on another app and will never need a supersedence relationship to a future version. Which app type lets the admin upload the MSI directly with no .intunewin packaging step?
options: A line-of-business (LOB) app
A Win32 app
The Microsoft Store app (new) type
A Microsoft 365 Apps deployment
questions.explanation: A line-of-business (LOB) app uploads a single installer file like an MSI directly to Intune with no .intunewin packaging step, which fits a simple install needing neither a dependency nor a future supersedence relationship. A Win32 app requires that packaging step in exchange for dependency and supersedence support this scenario doesn't need, the Microsoft Store app (new) type sources from the public store rather than an uploaded installer, and a Microsoft 365 Apps deployment is specifically for the Office suite, not a generic MSI.

questions.question: A company wants its app protection policy to automatically trigger a selective wipe of an app's corporate data if the app is ever launched on a device that has since become jailbroken. Which app protection policy setting category enforces that?
options: Data protection settings
Access requirements settings
Conditional launch settings
App configuration settings
questions.explanation: Conditional launch is the setting category that blocks or wipes an app's data when a defined condition, like a jailbroken device, is detected at launch. Data protection governs things like copy/paste and backup behavior, access requirements govern PIN and biometric prompts rather than triggering a wipe, and app configuration settings push values like a server URL rather than enforcing a security condition.

questions.question: A company wants Microsoft 365 Apps to receive new features on one predictable date each month, more often than a twice-yearly release but without the frequent changes of the fastest-moving channel. Which update channel fits?
options: Current Channel
Monthly Enterprise Channel
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
Beta Channel
questions.explanation: Monthly Enterprise Channel delivers new features once a month on a predictable, fixed date, sitting between the more frequent Current Channel and the twice-a-year Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel. Beta Channel is for early preview testing, not a predictable production release cadence.

questions.question: An organization already licenses base Intune but wants to add premium capabilities like Advanced Endpoint Analytics and Enterprise App Management without licensing each one as a separate standalone add-on. What should they look at?
options: Microsoft Intune Suite
Windows Autopatch
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Enterprise Mobility + Security E5
questions.explanation: Microsoft Intune Suite bundles several premium capabilities, including Advanced Endpoint Analytics and Enterprise App Management, under one add-on license rather than requiring each to be licensed separately. Autopatch is a separate update-management service, and Entra ID P2 and EMS E5 license identity and security features rather than these Intune-specific premium capabilities.

questions.question: A shared front-desk PC should sign a user straight into their own Cloud PC from the lock screen, rather than landing on the device's local desktop first. Which Windows 365 capability does this?
options: Windows 365 Switch
Windows 365 Boot
Windows 365 Frontline licensing
Autopilot Reset
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Boot lets a user sign in at the lock screen directly into their Cloud PC instead of the physical device's local desktop, matching the front-desk scenario. Windows 365 Switch instead moves a user between an already-signed-in local desktop and their Cloud PC, Frontline licensing is a Cloud PC licensing model rather than a sign-in behavior, and Autopilot Reset reprovisions a physical device rather than redirecting sign-in to a Cloud PC.

questions.question: A company wants a specific batch of devices, identified by serial number, marked as corporate-owned at enrollment so the right Company Portal experience and remote actions apply later, without changing how many devices any one user is allowed to enroll. What should be configured?
options: A device limit restriction
A corporate device identifiers list uploaded with those serial numbers
A platform enrollment restriction
A dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group
questions.explanation: A corporate device identifiers list marks specific hardware as corporate-owned by its serial number or IMEI at enrollment, independent of enrollment restrictions, which instead cap enrollment by platform or by per-user device count. A dynamic group affects policy targeting after enrollment, not ownership determination at enrollment.

questions.question: BitLocker's used space only encryption option encrypts every sector on the drive, including empty space, while full disk encryption encrypts only sectors that currently hold data.
questions.explanation: That description is reversed: used space only encrypts only sectors currently holding data and finishes faster, while full disk encryption also encrypts empty sectors, taking longer but leaving no unencrypted free space that could retain recoverable traces of deleted data.

questions.question: Windows Defender Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate cached domain credentials so that malware running with local administrator rights still cannot extract them.
questions.explanation: Credential Guard isolates cached domain credentials and NTLM hashes in a secured, virtualization-based enclave the operating system itself cannot reach, which is exactly why even administrator-level malware cannot extract reusable credentials from an infected device.

questions.question: The Win32 Content Prep Tool (IntuneWinAppUtil) must be run once per app version to produce the .intunewin file before that version can be uploaded as a Win32 app in Intune.
questions.explanation: Packaging with the Content Prep Tool happens once per version, outside the admin center, converting the setup folder into the encrypted .intunewin format Intune requires before that version can be uploaded, whether as a new app or a new version through supersedence.

questions.question: MAM without enrollment (MAM-WE) requires the target device to first complete full MDM enrollment before an app protection policy's controls can take effect.
questions.explanation: MAM-WE is specifically the scenario where app protection policy controls take effect with no MDM enrollment at all; the user only needs to be registered with Microsoft Entra ID, which is what makes it usable on a personal device the organization never manages.

questions.question: An Intune policy set lets several apps, configuration profiles, and compliance policies be bundled into one object and assigned to a group in a single step, instead of assigning each item separately.
questions.explanation: That is exactly what a policy set does, which is especially useful for onboarding a new department or location that needs the identical bundle of apps and policies every similar group already has.

questions.question: Autopilot for existing devices requires the OEM to have registered the device's hardware hash for Autopilot in advance, the same as a brand-new device purchased through a reseller.
questions.explanation: Autopilot for existing devices is specifically built to avoid that requirement: it converts an already-in-service device using a provisioning package built with Windows Configuration Designer, with no OEM hardware-hash registration needed in advance.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Microsoft Defender for Endpoint tamper protection and indicators policies? (Choose two.)
options: Tamper protection blocks core Defender Antivirus settings from being changed locally, even by a signed-in local administrator
An indicators policy can block a specific file, certificate, IP address, or URL by its exact identifier across onboarded devices
Tamper protection is configured per file hash, the same way an indicators policy is
Indicators policies can only allow items; they cannot block anything
questions.explanation: Tamper protection locks core Defender Antivirus settings against local changes even by a local administrator, and indicators policies block or allow specific files, certificates, IPs, or URLs by exact identifier across onboarded devices. Tamper protection and indicators are different mechanisms — tamper protection isn't scoped per file hash — and indicators support both allowing and blocking, not blocking alone.

questions.question: Which two of the following are true about Intune app packaging and deployment? (Choose two.)
options: A line-of-business (LOB) app uploads a single installer file directly with no .intunewin packaging step required
The Win32 Content Prep Tool must be run before a Win32 app's installer can be uploaded to Intune
A Win32 app and an LOB app require the exact same packaging process
Microsoft 365 Apps can only be deployed through a Win32 app package
questions.explanation: An LOB app skips the .intunewin packaging step entirely, while a Win32 app requires running the Content Prep Tool first to produce that .intunewin file before upload. LOB and Win32 apps have different packaging requirements, not the same process, and Microsoft 365 Apps has its own dedicated app type in Intune rather than needing to be packaged as a Win32 app.

lessons.title: Deploying and Updating Windows Devices
lessons.summary: Windows Autopilot and Windows 365 provisioning, plus Windows Update for Business rings, Autopatch, and safeguard holds.
lessons.reading:
Provisioning a new Windows device usually starts with Windows Autopilot, and picking the right deployment profile type is the first decision. A user-driven profile lets someone unbox their own laptop and sign in with their own Microsoft Entra ID account to finish setup. A self-deploying profile skips a human entirely and authenticates the device itself, which is why it needs a TPM 2.0 chip capable of proving identity with nobody there to sign in. A pre-provisioned, or white glove, profile lets a partner or IT complete the slow, time-consuming steps in advance, so the end user only finishes a short final phase. Whichever profile runs, the Enrollment Status Page blocks the desktop until required apps and configuration profiles finish installing, so a device only looks finished once it truly is ready for work. Underneath those classic profiles, Microsoft is steering new deployments toward device preparation, a newer, faster, cloud-native path — though it currently only supports Microsoft Entra joined devices, so a hybrid Entra joined deployment still needs a classic Autopilot profile. Getting new hardware into the right group before it even ships matters too: a group tag set during vendor reservation lets a dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group filter on it automatically, routing freshly registered hardware into the correct group and, through that group, the correct deployment profile, with no manual per-device assignment.

Cloud PCs follow a different provisioning path entirely. Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning policies decide which Microsoft Entra ID group receives a Cloud PC, which image it is built from, and whether it lands as Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid Entra joined — and it is what actually triggers Cloud PC creation once a user both holds a Windows 365 license and falls inside the policy's assigned group; having only one of the two produces no Cloud PC at all. Licensing itself comes in two shapes. Windows 365 Enterprise licenses one dedicated, always-on Cloud PC per named user, while Windows 365 Frontline licenses a smaller, shared pool of Cloud PCs across a larger set of shift-based users, capped at a limited number of concurrent connections per license set — the economical choice for shift workers, as long as no more of them are logged in at once than the license set allows.

Once a device is enrolled, keeping it current becomes its own discipline. Update rings are the core policy: they set deferral periods, whether updates install automatically, active hours, and whether a device sits in an early or broad deployment wave, commonly staged so a small pilot ring with a short or zero deferral catches a bad update before it reaches a much larger, longer-deferral ring. Two different deferral clocks run independently inside the same ring. Feature update deferral delays a new annual Windows version by up to 365 days, while quality update deferral delays that same month's cumulative security fixes by up to 30 days — delaying one never delays the other, so a device can sit on a much older Windows version while still receiving this month's patches on time. For organizations that would rather not hand-tune rings at all, Windows Autopatch takes over entirely: it automatically organizes enrolled, already Intune-managed devices into deployment rings and rolls out Windows quality updates, driver and firmware updates, Microsoft 365 Apps updates, and Edge updates on Microsoft's own schedule. Autopatch-eligible devices can also pick up Hotpatch updates, which apply a subset of security fixes to a running instance in memory with no reboot at all — though a Hotpatch device still periodically lands on a fresh baseline cumulative update, since not every fix can be applied purely in memory, so it reduces reboots rather than eliminating them.

Not every update rollout is voluntary from the administrator's side, either. A safeguard hold is Microsoft's own protective mechanism: when Microsoft detects a known compatibility issue between a feature update and a specific device, it automatically blocks that device from being offered the upgrade until the issue is resolved or an admin deliberately overrides the hold — prevention before the update ever lands, distinct from a rollback that removes an update after it already landed and caused a problem.
